All objective components are minimized and can be combined exactly.
Dominance pruning compares only mutually compatible partial assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is exactly the global Pareto set \(P\).
review_flags: No target-specific authoritative source or locator was supplied for complete multiobjective DCOP methods.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports this generic algorithm or its completeness claim. Dominance pruning of compatible partial assignments is safe only under algorithm-specific state-equivalence and extension conditions that are not stated.

children.title: Pareto Approximation
children.top_down_role: Approximate representations of nondominated multiobjective solution sets.

knowledge_statements.title: Pareto Approximation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Multiplicative approximation of a positive minimization Pareto frontier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(Y=F(X)\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}^m\) be the attainable objective set of a minimization problem and let \(Y^*\) be its nondominated subset. For \(\varepsilon\geq0\), a finite set \(A\subseteq Y\) is a multiplicative \(\varepsilon\)-Pareto approximation if, for every \(y\in Y^*\), there exists \(a\in A\) satisfying \(a_j\leq(1+\varepsilon)y_j\) for every \(j\in\{1,\ldots,m\}\). Requiring \(A\subseteq Y\) ensures that every reported vector is attainable; when \(\varepsilon=0\), the definition requires an attainable vector weakly dominating every Pareto vector.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An epsilon-Pareto approximation is an attainable finite set containing, componentwise, a vector within factor one plus epsilon of every Pareto-optimal vector.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}^m\) and all components are minimized.
\(\varepsilon\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(A\) covers every \(y\in Y^*\) within coordinatewise factor \(1+\varepsilon\).
review_flags: No relevant multiobjective optimization source was supplied for the selected multiplicative convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The multiplicative approximation definition is mathematically coherent and fits the leaf, but no source with an inspectable locator supports the selected convention.

children.title: Distributed Pareto Search
children.top_down_role: Distributed search families targeting nondominated solutions.

knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Pareto Search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed enumeration with compatibility checks and sound dominance pruning.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite multiobjective DCOP and a rooted communication structure. Each agent initializes labels for its locally feasible assignments, where a label records a separator assignment, an accumulated objective vector, and compatible witnesses. Agents repeatedly exchange labels, join labels agreeing on shared variables, add their objective vectors without double-counting local costs, and remove a label only if another label with the same separator assignment weakly dominates it. After every message has been processed and no label can change, the root outputs its nondominated labels and propagates their witnesses to reconstruct global assignments. With reliable delivery and exhaustive label generation, the output is the exact Pareto set; optional approximation pruning replaces exact completeness by its stated coverage guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents exchange compatible partial solutions, prune dominance only within identical interfaces, and reconstruct the globally nondominated assignments when distributed label propagation becomes quiescent.
assumptions_latex: Variables and domains are finite.
Messages are delivered reliably and objective aggregation avoids double counting.
Exact mode generates every compatible label before termination.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exact mode returns all and only globally Pareto-optimal assignments and objective vectors.
review_flags: The statement specifies a generic exact label-search family; no algorithm-specific DCOP source was supplied.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but the exactness claim depends on an unspecified distributed label algorithm, separator invariant, termination rule, and reconstruction theorem. No relevant source is cited.

children.title: Approximation–Search Quality Regimes
children.top_down_role: Quality boundaries linking Pareto-set approximation to distributed search coverage.

knowledge_statements.title: Approximation–Search Quality Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Guarantee boundary between exact search, certified approximation, and heuristic truncation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite minimization objective set \(Y\subset\mathbb{R}_{>0}^m\), distributed Pareto search has three distinct quality regimes. If pruning removes only dominated labels and search is exhaustive, its output is \(Y^*\). If pruning preserves an explicit multiplicative cover with tolerance \(\varepsilon>0\), its attainable output \(A\) satisfies \(\forall y\in Y^*\,\exists a\in A\,\forall j:\ a_j\leq(1+\varepsilon)y_j\). If labels are instead discarded solely because of a fixed memory, beam-width, or time cap, neither exactness nor any uniform finite approximation factor follows without an additional invariant. Thus resource truncation alone is not an approximation certificate.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Exhaustive dominance search is exact; cover-preserving pruning is epsilon-approximate; an arbitrary beam, memory, or time cap supplies no Pareto-quality guarantee by itself.
assumptions_latex: \(Y\) is finite and contained in \(\mathbb{R}_{>0}^m\).
All objective components are minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Only exhaustive search or a maintained cover invariant yields the corresponding stated quality guarantee.
review_flags: No source was supplied for this exact classification of distributed approximation and resource-truncation regimes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the comparison of quality regimes, but no source supports the exact classification or the universal no-guarantee assertion for arbitrary resource truncation.

children.title: Agent Changes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic DCOP regimes involving agent arrival, departure, or role change.

knowledge_statements.title: Agent Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic DCOP events that alter participating agents or ownership.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Represent a dynamic DCOP at time \(t\) by an agent set \(A_t\), variable set \(V_t\), and ownership map \(o_t:V_t\to A_t\). An agent change occurs between \(t\) and \(t+1\) when \(A_{t+1}\neq A_t\), or when the restriction of the ownership relation to surviving variables changes because variables are transferred to, or from, joining or departing agents. A valid transition additionally specifies the disposition of every variable and constraint owned by a departing agent, so that the instance at \(t+1\) is well formed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent change adds or removes participants, or reassigns variable ownership, while specifying how affected variables and constraints persist, transfer, or disappear.
assumptions_latex: Each \(o_t\) is a total ownership map on \(V_t\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition is an agent change when \(A_t\) or the relevant ownership relation changes.

notation.meaning: decision variables present at time t

review_flags: No authoritative dynamic-DCOP taxonomy source was supplied for agent changes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No dynamic-DCOP taxonomy source supports treating both participant-set changes and ownership reassignment as agent changes. The selected convention therefore cannot be validated.

children.title: Domain Changes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic regimes involving changes to variable domains.

knowledge_statements.title: Domain Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic events altering the admissible values of persistent variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a dynamic DCOP have variables \(V_t\) with nonempty finite domains \(D_i^t\) at time \(t\). A domain change between \(t\) and \(t+1\) occurs when some persistent variable \(i\in V_t\cap V_{t+1}\) satisfies \(D_i^{t+1}\neq D_i^t\). Values in \(D_i^{t+1}\setminus D_i^t\) are additions and values in \(D_i^t\setminus D_i^{t+1}\) are removals. Removing a currently selected value invalidates that assignment and requires selecting a value in the new domain; an empty new domain makes the updated instance infeasible.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A domain change adds or removes admissible values of a persistent variable; deleting its selected value invalidates the assignment, and an empty domain causes infeasibility.
assumptions_latex: Each domain \(D_i^t\) is finite.
The variable \(i\) persists across the transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A domain change is characterized by \(D_i^{t+1}\neq D_i^t\) for at least one persistent variable.

notation.meaning: domain of variable i at time t

review_flags: No authoritative dynamic-DCOP taxonomy source was supplied for domain changes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally precise and fits the leaf, but no authoritative dynamic-DCOP source with a locator supports this classification and its infeasibility consequence.

children.title: Constraint Changes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic regimes involving changes to constraint presence or content.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic events altering constraint presence, scope, feasibility, or cost values.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write the DCOP constraint family at time \(t\) as \(C_t=\{(S_c^t,f_c^t):c\in I_t\}\), where \(S_c^t\) is a variable scope and \(f_c^t\) maps scope assignments to costs, possibly including \(+\infty\) for forbidden assignments. A constraint change occurs when a constraint identifier is added or removed, or when a persistent constraint has \(S_c^{t+1}\neq S_c^t\) or differs in value on some assignment common to both versions. Consequently, changes to hard feasibility and changes to soft costs are both constraint changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A constraint change adds or removes a constraint, changes its scope, or changes a hard-feasibility or soft-cost value on some local assignment.
assumptions_latex: Every constraint has a specified finite scope and cost table or evaluable cost function.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The constraint family changes exactly when its identifiers, scopes, or represented cost functions differ.
review_flags: No authoritative dynamic-DCOP taxonomy source was supplied for constraint changes.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition coherently covers additions, removals, scope changes, and value changes, but the claimed dynamic-DCOP taxonomy has no supporting citation.

children.title: Topology Changes
children.top_down_role: Dynamic regimes involving changes to interaction or communication structure.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology Changes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic events altering interaction or communication edges among persistent entities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_t=(U_t,E_t)\) denote a DCOP interaction graph or an explicitly modeled communication graph at time \(t\). A topology change between \(t\) and \(t+1\) occurs when, after identifying persistent vertices, the edge relation changes: \(E_{t+1}\neq E_t\). In an interaction graph, an edge records co-occurrence of variables or agents in a constraint; in a communication graph, it records an available communication link. The graph convention must be fixed before classifying the event because changing communication reachability need not change the optimization constraints, and conversely.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A topology change adds or removes interaction or communication edges among persistent entities; the chosen graph semantics must be stated because the two notions differ.
assumptions_latex: The meaning of vertices and edges is fixed across the transition.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The transition is topological precisely when the corresponding edge relation changes.

notation.meaning: interaction or communication graph at time t

review_flags: No source was supplied to select a single interaction-topology or communication-topology convention.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement leaves topology as either an interaction graph or a communication graph, which are materially different conventions. A target-specific source is needed to determine the intended local meaning.

knowledge_statements.title: Stability-Aware Dynamic Models
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Dynamic objectives combining current solution quality with transition disruption.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F_t(x)\) be the aggregate DCOP cost at time \(t\), let \(x^{t-1}\) be the previously implemented assignment, and let \(d_t(x,x^{t-1})\geq0\) quantify disruption. A stability-aware update selects \(x^t\in X_t\) by \[x^t\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\in X_t}\bigl(F_t(x)+\lambda_t d_t(x,x^{t-1})\bigr),\] where \(\lambda_t\geq0\). Equivalently, a constrained form minimizes \(F_t(x)\) subject to \(d_t(x,x^{t-1})\leq B_t\). The penalty or budget makes persistence explicit: \(\lambda_t=0\) recovers pure reoptimization, while larger penalties discourage assignment changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A stability-aware dynamic model balances current DCOP cost against disruption from the previous assignment, using either a switching penalty or a disruption budget.
assumptions_latex: \(X_t\) is the current feasible assignment set.
\(d_t\) is nonnegative and vanishes when no modeled change occurs.
\(\lambda_t\geq0\) or \(B_t\geq0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The selected assignment optimizes current quality subject to an explicit stability tradeoff.
review_flags: No stability-aware dynamic-DCOP source was supplied for the penalty and budget formulations.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation fits stability-aware dynamic models, but no source supports these particular penalty and budget formulations. They are alternative models and are not generally equivalent without additional assumptions or parameter correspondence.

knowledge_statements.title: S-DPOP Family
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Self-stabilizing DPOP-style recomputation after transient faults or dynamic changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Input a finite DCOP and a distributed state that may contain stale pseudo-tree, utility, or value information. Each agent repeatedly validates its parent, children, separator, version data, and received messages against current neighbors and constraints. Invalid dependent state is discarded. Once its descendants' current utility messages are available, a nonroot agent recomputes and sends its utility projection to its parent; the root chooses an optimal root value, and current value messages propagate downward so each agent chooses a minimizing local value consistent with its separator assignment. The algorithm stops operationally when no enabled correction or message update remains. Under a fixed instance and fair reliable execution, legitimate quiescent states encode a DPOP-optimal assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: S-DPOP-style agents detect stale distributed state, rebuild valid dependencies, recompute utility messages, and propagate values until a fixed DCOP reaches an optimal legitimate state.

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_C=(V,E_C)\) be the ordinary DCOP interaction graph. knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource-aware pseudo-tree is built on the interaction graph after adding edges between decisions that affect a common resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Aware Pseudo-Trees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source confirms that resource-aware pseudo-trees are formed by clique-completing every resource scope or that the resulting separators have the stated interpretation. The definition kind otherwise fits the leaf.

children.title: Resource-Free Pseudo-Trees
children.top_down_role: Pseudo-tree structures formed without explicit resource relationships.

assumptions_latex: The ordinary constraint interaction graph is finite and connected.
Resource dependencies are stored separately from ordinary constraint edges.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Every edge in \(E_C\setminus E(T)\) joins an ancestor-descendant pair, without imposing this condition on resource-induced edges.

notation.meaning: Rooted spanning tree of the ordinary interaction graph

review_flags: No supplied source defines the resource-free/resource-aware pseudo-tree distinction.
Confirm that resource-free means construction from ordinary constraint edges only.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Pseudo-tree ignoring resource-induced adjacency during construction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G_C=(V,E_C)\) be the graph containing an edge exactly when two variables occur together in an ordinary DCOP cost or constraint. A resource-free pseudo-tree is a rooted spanning tree \(T\) of \(G_C\) such that every non-tree edge in \(E_C\) connects a vertex to an ancestor. Resource memberships and capacity constraints do not add edges when \(T\) is constructed. Consequently, resource-coupled variables may lie in incomparable branches and must be coordinated by a separate resource-accounting mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A resource-free pseudo-tree uses only ordinary constraint interactions; variables sharing a resource may therefore occur in separate branches.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Free Pseudo-Trees

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ordinary-graph pseudo-tree definition is coherent, but no source establishes that this is the intended meaning of “resource-free” or supports the asserted separate-accounting consequence.

children.title: Resource-Induced Structural Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Structural consequences of incorporating resource relationships into pseudo-trees.

assumptions_latex: Both pseudo-trees are evaluated by the same elimination or dynamic-programming scheme.
Message scope is determined by ancestor separators in the selected graph.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Resource augmentation can enlarge structural width while making every resource scope structurally explicit; neither effect universally dominates the other.

notation.meaning: Induced separator width of a pseudo-tree T on graph G

review_flags: The qualitative tradeoff is structurally plausible but lacks a supplied DCOP-specific source.
Algorithm-dependent communication and memory consequences require source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Structural comparison between resource-aware and resource-free decompositions.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Because \(E_C\subseteq E_C\cup E_R\), adding resource-induced edges cannot decrease the minimum induced width over a fixed set of elimination orders: \[\min_T w_{G^+}(T)\ge 
\min_T w_{G_C}(T).\] A resource-aware pseudo-tree exposes every shared-resource interaction inside its ancestor separators, simplifying exact local accounting but potentially increasing separator size. A resource-free pseudo-tree can retain smaller ordinary separators, but a resource whose scope intersects incomparable branches then requires additional cross-branch state, messages, or relaxation. Hence the preferable structure depends jointly on graph width and resource-scope placement.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding resource edges can increase separator width but makes resource dependencies explicit; omitting them may reduce width while requiring extra cross-branch coordination.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource-Induced Structural Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The qualitative tradeoff is plausible, but the ranges of the two minima over \(T\) are not defined consistently, and the message, separator, and coordination consequences depend on the particular DCOP algorithm. A domain-specific source is required.

children.title: Multiple Constraint Models
children.top_down_role: DCOP variants governed by multiple concurrent global or local restrictions.

assumptions_latex: Variables have nonempty finite domains.
Each constraint has a finite variable scope and an extended-real local evaluation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model objective is \(F(x)=\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{c\in C_k}f_{k,c}(x_c)\), with feasibility encoded by finite total value.

notation.meaning: Constraint collection belonging to model k
Evaluation of constraint c in model k

review_flags: The supplied general modeling locators do not identify the DCOP extension called Multiple Constraint Models.
Confirm whether models are simultaneous layers, alternatives, or dynamically selected regimes.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Simultaneous layered constraint models over shared distributed variables.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(K\) index constraint models defined over common variables \(x_i\in D_i\). Model \(k\) consists of scoped functions \(\{f_{k,c}:\prod_{i\in c}D_i\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}:c\in C_k\}\). A simultaneous multiple-constraint DCOP minimizes \[F(x)=\sum_{k\in K}\sum_{c\in C_k}f_{k,c}(x_c).\] Hard constraints are represented by \(+\infty\), so a complete assignment is feasible exactly when \(F(x)<+\infty\). Distinct models may encode different constraint classes or operating layers while retaining distributed ownership of variables and functions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Multiple constraint models are simultaneous layers of scoped evaluations over shared variables, combined into one objective with infinite values encoding violations.
knowledge_statements.title: Multiple Constraint Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No citation establishes that “Multiple Constraint Models” means simultaneous additive layers rather than alternative or dynamically selected models. That unresolved distinction determines the correct mathematical definition.

children.title: Resource–Constraint Coupling
children.top_down_role: Structural interactions between resource limits and additional constraint families.

assumptions_latex: Every resource load is determined by the assignments of variables in its scope.
Each resource evaluator is defined on all attainable loads.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The coupled objective is \(F(x)=\sum_{c\in C}f_c(x_c)+\sum_{r\in R}q_r(L_r(x))\).
review_flags: No supplied locator directly supports the resource-constraint coupling formalism in DCOPs.
The intended coupling may distinguish hard capacities from soft congestion costs.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Objective-level coupling of ordinary constraints and resource evaluations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let ordinary constraints contribute \(f_c(x_c)\), and for each resource \(r\in R\) let \(L_r(x_{S_r})\) be the load induced by variables in scope \(S_r\). Resource-constraint coupling is represented by \[F(x)=\sum_{c\in C}f_c(x_c)+\sum_{r\in R}q_r\bigl(L_r(x_{S_r})\bigr),\] where \(q_r:\mathbb{R}_{\ge0}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) evaluates the resource state. The coupling is hard when \(q_r(ell)=+\infty\) beyond capacity and soft when overload receives a finite penalty. Variables in \(S_r\) are coupled even if they share no ordinary constraint.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Resource-constraint coupling adds a resource evaluation of aggregate load to ordinary local costs, creating dependencies among all decisions affecting that resource.
knowledge_statements.title: Resource–Constraint Coupling

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation kind fits the proposed objective coupling, but no DCOP source supports this exact formalism or its hard/soft interpretation. The statement also uses "ell" where the load variable should be \(\ell\).

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: ODPOP: An Algorithm for Open/Distributed Constraint Optimization

children.title: Open Domain Models
children.top_down_role: DCOP models permitting domain content to remain extensible or incompletely enumerated.

assumptions_latex: At every stage each revealed domain is finite and nonempty.
Previously revealed values remain available at later stages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: An open domain model satisfies \(D_i^{(t)}\subseteq D_i^{(t+1)}\) for all variables \(i\) and stages \(t\).

notation.meaning: Values of variable i revealed by stage t

review_flags: The supplied sources do not define open DCOP domains.
Confirm whether openness means monotone value revelation, agent arrival, or both.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Monotone, stagewise revelation of finite variable domains.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For discrete stages \(t=0,1,2,\ldots\), an open domain model assigns each variable \(x_i\) a revealed finite domain \(D_i^{(t)}\) satisfying \[\varnothing\ne D_i^{(t)}\subseteq D_i^{(t+1)}.\] The stage-
\(t\) DCOP is optimized over \(X^{(t)}=\prod_i D_i^{(t)}\), using the restrictions of the cost functions to revealed assignments. Newly revealed values enlarge the feasible assignment set but do not remove earlier values. A stage solution is therefore provisional unless a stopping or stability condition certifies that future revelations cannot improve it.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An open domain model reveals finite sets of values over time, preserves previously revealed values, and treats each stage optimum as potentially provisional.
knowledge_statements.title: Open Domain Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No source establishes that open DCOP domains specifically mean monotone value revelation with persistent values. Openness may instead include agent, variable, or constraint arrival, so the proposed definition cannot yet be fixed.

children.title: Unbounded Domain Models
children.top_down_role: DCOP models whose domains lack fixed finite bounds.

assumptions_latex: Every finite stage exposes a finite nonempty domain.
Domain revelation is monotone.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The model is unbounded exactly when \(\sup_t|D_i^{(t)}|=+\infty\) for at least one variable \(i\).

notation.meaning: Limit domain revealed over all stages

review_flags: No supplied source fixes the intended meaning of unbounded domain in open DCOPs.
Verify whether unbounded refers to cardinality, numerical magnitude, or unknown finite size.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Unbounded cardinal growth under finite stagewise revelation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An expanding-domain DCOP is an unbounded domain model when each stage domain \(D_i^{(t)}\) is finite, \(D_i^{(t)}\subseteq D_i^{(t+1)}\), and for at least one variable \(i\), \[\sup_{t\ge0}|D_i^{(t)}|=+\infty.\] Equivalently, its limit domain \(D_i^{(\infty)}=igcup_{t\ge0}D_i^{(t)}\) is infinite. Unboundedness concerns the absence of a uniform finite cardinality bound across stages; it does not require any single stage to contain an infinite domain.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An expanding domain is unbounded when some variable gains arbitrarily many values over time, although every individual stage may remain finite.
knowledge_statements.title: Unbounded Domain Models

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is required to decide whether “unbounded” concerns cardinality, numerical extent, or unknown finite size. The limit-domain formula is also malformed: "igcup" must be \(\bigcup\).

children.title: Domain-Growth Boundaries
children.top_down_role: Applicability limits associated with expanding or nonfinite domains.

assumptions_latex: Revealed domains expand monotonically.
The stage objective is the restriction of one fixed extended-real objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Finite stabilization certifies the limit optimum; without stabilization or an exclusion bound, no finite-stage optimum is generally final.
review_flags: The boundary statement follows standard expanding-feasible-set reasoning but lacks an open-DCOP source.
Literature may impose a different termination or bounded-growth condition.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Boundary between finite stabilization and indefinitely improvable domain growth.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For minimization over nested feasible sets \(X^{(t)}\subseteq X^{(t+1)}\), the values \(v_t=
inf_{x\in X^{(t)}}F(x)\) satisfy \(v_{t+1}\le v_t\). If some \(T\) satisfies \(X^{(t)}=X^{(T)}\) for every \(t\ge T\), then \(v_T=\inf_{x\in X^{(\infty)}}F(x)\). Without such stabilization, or a valid lower bound proving that every unrevealed assignment has cost at least \(v_t\), finite-stage optimality need not imply limit optimality. For example, revealing at stage \(t\) a new value of cost \(1/(t+1)\) strictly improves every preceding stage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Stage optima improve monotonically, but no finite-stage solution is final unless domains stabilize or a bound excludes improvement by unrevealed values.
knowledge_statements.title: Domain-Growth Boundaries

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The expanding-feasible-set observation is standard, but no open-DCOP source confirms that stabilization or the proposed exclusion bound is the intended terminal boundary. The definition of \(v_t\) also contains malformed TeX, rendering "inf" instead of \(\inf\).

assumptions_latex: The open DCOP reveals only finitely many new values per update.
Each finite-stage subproblem admits an exact pseudo-tree dynamic-programming solution.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After every finite update, the maintained solution is optimal for the currently revealed DCOP; global termination additionally requires a domain-closure certificate.

notation.meaning: Values revealed for variable i at stage t

review_flags: The acronym ODPOP and its canonical update rules cannot be resolved reliably from the supplied sources.
A primary ODPOP source is required before fixing message semantics, reuse rules, and termination conditions.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional incremental pseudo-tree interpretation pending a primary ODPOP source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize with revealed domains \(D_i^{(0)}\), a pseudo-tree, and an exact dynamic-programming solve producing \(x^{(0)}\). At update \(t+1\), incorporate each newly revealed value into \(D_i^{(t+1)}\), recompute affected local cost tables, invalidate every cached message whose scope contains changed information, and propagate revised utility messages toward the root followed by value choices toward the leaves. Output \(x^{(t+1)}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{x\inrak X^{(t+1)}}F^{(t+1)}(x)\). Stop globally only when a domain-closure certificate establishes that no further value can be revealed; otherwise report the current-stage optimum and continue receiving updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Provisionally, ODPOP incrementally repairs pseudo-tree dynamic-programming messages after domain growth and returns an exact optimum for each revealed finite stage.
knowledge_statements.title: ODPOP Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ODPOP update, cache invalidation, message-repair, exactness, and termination rules are explicitly provisional and cannot be validated without a primary ODPOP source. The statement additionally contains the invalid command \(\inrak\), and \(X^{(t+1)}\) is not introduced in the statement.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: New Algorithms for Functional Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems
top_down_textbook_witnesses.locator: Functional DCOP model and exact/approximate families
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: New Algorithms for Functional Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems

assumptions_latex: Each agent controls designated variables, and every cost function has a finite agent scope.
The global objective is the sum of the local costs wherever all summands are defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The represented solution is any globally feasible minimizer of \(F(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal F}f_\alpha(x_{S_\alpha})\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional representation with arbitrary variable domains and additive scoped costs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A functional distributed constraint optimization problem consists of variables \(x_i\in D_i\), an ownership map assigning each variable to an agent, and scoped functions \(f_\alpha:\prod_{i\in S_\alpha}D_i\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). An assignment \(x\in\prod_iD_i\) is feasible when \(f_\alpha(x_{S_\alpha})<+\infty\) for every hard-constraint function. Its objective value is \[F(x)=\sum_{\alpha\in\mathcal F}f_\alpha(x_{S_\alpha}),\] and solving the representation means finding a feasible \(x^\star\) satisfying \(F(x^\star)=\inf_x F(x)\), with each function stored or evaluated by agents that know its scope.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A functional DCOP assigns variables to agents and minimizes the sum of scoped real-valued cost functions, using infinite cost to encode forbidden assignments.
knowledge_statements.title: Functional DCOP Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the functional-DCOP representation leaf and is broadly plausible, but no source supports the DCOP ownership, scoped-function, feasibility, or distributed-storage formulation. The distinction between hard-constraint functions and other functions also requires an explicit sourced definition.

assumptions_latex: Every continuous variable has a nonempty subset of Euclidean space as its domain.
Agents can evaluate their incident functions and communicate information permitted by the selected method.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Continuous DCOP methods seek a feasible \(x^\star\) attaining, or approximately attaining, \(\inf_{x\in D}F(x)\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Method-family criterion for functional DCOPs whose decision domains are continuous.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a functional DCOP on \(D\subseteq\mathbb R^n\), a continuous DCOP method generates agent-local states and messages whose decoded assignment \(\widehat x\in D\) respects all hard constraints. An exact method must terminate only with \(F(\widehat x)=\inf_{x\in D}F(x)\). An \(\varepsilon\)-accurate method may instead terminate with \[F(\widehat x)\leq\inf_{x\in D}F(x)+\varepsilon.\] Method families differ in the regularity assumed of local functions and in whether messages communicate samples, analytic function pieces, derivatives, bounds, or finite approximations; any claimed guarantee is conditional on those assumptions and the stated communication model.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Continuous DCOP methods coordinate agents over Euclidean domains and must state whether they return exact optima or assignments within a specified objective tolerance.
knowledge_statements.title: Continuous DCOP Method Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits a continuous-DCOP method-family container, but no source establishes this family characterization or the exact and additive-epsilon guarantees. Conditions such as a finite lower objective value, attainability for exact termination, and method-specific regularity assumptions cannot be resolved reliably without an authoritative source.

assumptions_latex: At least one decision block is integer-valued and at least one is continuous-valued.
Each local cost depends only on its declared agent scope.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A solution minimizes the sum of local functions over the mixed-integer feasible set.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Mixed-integer functional formulation, independent of any particular distributed solution method.

source_refs.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_refs.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mixed-integer functional DCOP has an agent-owned integer block \(z\in Z\subseteq\mathbb Z^p\), an agent-owned continuous block \(y\in Y\subseteq\mathbb R^q\), and scoped functions \(f_\alpha(z_{S_\alpha},y_{S_\alpha})\in\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Its feasible set is \[\mathcal X=\{(z,y)\in Z\times Y:f_\alpha(z_{S_\alpha},y_{S_\alpha})<+\infty\text{ for every hard-constraint function}\}.\] A solution \((z^\star,y^\star)\in\mathcal X\) satisfies \[\sum_\alpha f_\alpha(z^\star_{S_\alpha},y^\star_{S_\alpha})=\inf_{(z,y)\in\mathcal X}\sum_\alpha f_\alpha(z_{S_\alpha},y_{S_\alpha}).\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mixed-integer functional DCOP distributes integer and continuous variables among agents and minimizes the sum of scoped functions over their joint feasible set.
knowledge_statements.title: Mixed-Integer Functional DCOPs

source_witnesses.locator: 1.1 The structured nonconvex mixed integer nonlinear program p. 3
source_witnesses.source_title: Relaxation and Decomposition Methods for Mixed Integer Nonlinear Programming

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The mixed-integer formulation fits the leaf and the cited section can support a generic structured mixed-integer nonlinear model, but it does not establish the DCOP-specific agent ownership, distributed scopes, or functional representation. A DCOP-specific source with a precise locator is required.

assumptions_latex: The distributed constraint satisfaction problem has finite domains and reliable eventual message delivery.
Agents have a fixed total priority order and each agent owns one variable.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Termination with compatible agent views yields a solution; derivation of the empty nogood certifies inconsistency.

notation.meaning: agent i's assignments for higher-priority neighbors

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical finite-domain asynchronous backtracking for distributed constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each agent \(i\) initializes a value \(v_i\) consistent with its higher-priority agent view \(V_i\) and sends the assignment to lower-priority neighbors. On receiving an assignment or nogood, it updates \(V_i\) and deletes values ruled out by stored nogoods. If some value remains consistent, it selects one and announces it. Otherwise it resolves the explanations excluding all values into a nogood \(N\), sends \(N\) to the lowest-priority agent occurring in \(N\), and removes obsolete lower-priority assignments from its view. The algorithm stops with a solution when all constraints are satisfied and messages quiesce, or reports unsatisfiability when the empty nogood is derived.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents asynchronously exchange assignments and logically valid nogoods, backtracking toward higher-priority agents when every local value is excluded.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Backtracking

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct content kind, but the precise agent-view updates, nogood construction and recipient rule, quiescence test, and empty-nogood behavior depend on the canonical asynchronous-backtracking protocol. No inspectable source is supplied.

assumptions_latex: Variables have finite domains, messages are eventually delivered, and recorded nogoods are logically valid.
Each agent maintains a unique dynamically changeable priority.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A stable globally consistent assignment is returned as a solution; an empty nogood establishes unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Weak-commitment extension of asynchronous backtracking with dynamic priorities.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each agent initializes a value and priority, exchanges assignments with constrained neighbors, and maintains nogoods \(\mathcal N_i\). After updating its agent view, a conflicted agent first selects a value minimizing violations with lower-priority assignments while remaining consistent with higher-priority assignments. If no such value exists, it constructs a valid nogood from the conflicting higher-priority assignments, raises its priority above the priorities in its current view, chooses a minimum-conflict value under the resulting order, and broadcasts its new priority and assignment. Obsolete view entries are discarded. Execution stops when all agents' announced values are mutually consistent and communication quiesces, or when an empty nogood is generated.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weak-commitment search extends asynchronous backtracking by raising a blocked agent's priority and choosing a value that minimizes conflicts under the revised order.
knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Weak-Commitment Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for this leaf, but the ordering of minimum-conflict selection, nogood generation, priority raising, broadcasts, and obsolete-view deletion is protocol-specific and cannot be validated from standard-field rationale alone.

assumptions_latex: The distributed constraint satisfaction problem has finite domains and nonnegative weights on violated constraints.
Agents can detect local minima and reliably exchange current assignments and weight changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The output is a satisfying assignment when the weighted violation value reaches \(0\); otherwise iteration continues.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Distributed weighted local-repair scheme for finite-domain satisfaction problems.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize every constraint weight by \(w_c=1\) and choose an assignment \(x\). Define \[E_w(x)=\sum_{c\text{ violated by }x}w_c.\] Using exchanged neighbor assignments, each agent computes the decrease in \(E_w\) obtainable by changing its value. A conflict-free coordination rule selects a set of compatible improving changes, which are applied concurrently. If no admissible change has positive decrease while some constraint remains violated, the agents increase \(w_c\) for the currently violated constraints and resume local repair. The algorithm outputs \(x\) when \(E_w(x)=0\); without additional assumptions, failure to reach zero does not certify unsatisfiability.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Distributed breakout performs coordinated local repair and increases the weights of currently violated constraints whenever search reaches a non-solution local minimum.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Breakout

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record describes a plausible distributed breakout family, but the compatible-move coordination rule and the rule that increases every currently violated constraint weight are variant-dependent. A canonical distributed-breakout source is needed to identify the intended algorithm.

assumptions_latex: All variable domains are finite.
Constraint information and domain deletions are eventually delivered to every agent responsible for an affected constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: At quiescence every retained value has the required local support; an empty domain certifies inconsistency of the original problem.

notation.meaning: binary constraint between variables i and j
support set in the neighboring domain

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic asynchronous distributed arc-consistency propagation for binary finite-domain constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each directed constrained pair \((i,j)\) and value \(a\in D_i\), define \[S_{ij}(a)=\{b\in D_j:(a,b)\in C_{ij}\}.\] Agents initialize their current domains and exchange them with constraint neighbors. Whenever an agent learns that \(S_{ij}(a)\cap D_j=\varnothing\), it deletes \(a\) from \(D_i\) and communicates the deletion to affected neighbors. Processing continues asynchronously until no message can cause another deletion. The resulting domains are arc consistent because every retained value has support across every incident binary constraint. If some \(D_i=\varnothing\), the original problem is inconsistent; nonempty arc-consistent domains need not constitute a solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents repeatedly communicate domain deletions until every retained value has support across each incident binary constraint; an empty domain proves inconsistency.
knowledge_statements.title: Distributed Consistency Algorithms

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The arc-consistency propagation claim is mathematically plausible and algorithm is a suitable kind, but the leaf covers distributed consistency algorithms while the record selects one generic binary asynchronous arc-consistency variant. A specific authoritative variant and its communication and termination conditions must be cited.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains, nonnegative finite costs, and a fixed total ordering of its agents.
Messages are reliable and partial-assignment cost lower bounds are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the search frontier is exhausted, the incumbent assignment has minimum global cost.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Synchronous depth-first distributed branch-and-bound along a total agent order.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize the incumbent bound by \(U=+\infty\) and pass an empty partial assignment \(P\) to the first agent. Agent \(i\) considers its values sequentially, appends \(x_i=v\) to \(P\), and computes an admissible bound \(L(P)\) on every completion. If \(L(P)\geq U\), that branch is pruned; otherwise the extended assignment is passed to the next agent. A complete assignment of cost below \(U\) becomes the incumbent and its cost is broadcast. When an agent exhausts its values, control returns to its predecessor. After the first agent exhausts all branches, the incumbent is returned as a globally optimal solution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: SyncBB passes one partial assignment synchronously through an agent order, pruning any branch whose admissible lower bound cannot improve the incumbent.
knowledge_statements.title: SyncBB Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithm role matches the SyncBB leaf, but this generic depth-first branch-and-bound account does not document the canonical SyncBB cost accounting, messages, incumbent propagation, or termination protocol. Those details and the optimality conclusion require a primary source.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains and a fixed agent order.
Every pruning bound is a lower bound on the cost of all completions of the associated partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Exhaustive bounded search returns an optimal assignment, provided the family's no-commitment message protocol preserves every unpruned branch.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Provisional generic characterization; the canonical NCBB protocol requires source confirmation.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(U=+\infty\). Agents enumerate finite-domain assignments in the fixed order while communicating each candidate partial assignment \(P\), its accumulated cost, and an admissible completion bound \(L(P)\). A branch may be discarded only when \(L(P)\geq U\). Any complete assignment with cost below \(U\) replaces the incumbent and causes the improved bound to be disseminated. The no-commitment protocol must retain sufficient identifiers and search state to prevent delayed messages from deleting or duplicating an unpruned branch. The algorithm terminates after every branch is either evaluated or validly pruned and then returns the incumbent; the precise NCBB message and synchronization rules remain variant-dependent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: NCBB performs distributed bounded enumeration without irrevocably committing agents to a single partial assignment; exact protocol details require a canonical source.
knowledge_statements.title: NCBB Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The candidate explicitly gives only a provisional generic bounded-enumeration scheme. Without a canonical NCBB source, neither the intended expansion nor the defining no-commitment protocol, message state, duplicate prevention, and termination rule can be established reliably.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains, nonnegative costs, a total agent order, and reliable asynchronous delivery.
Each forward-bound estimate is admissible for the unassigned suffix.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: After all generated branches are completed or validly pruned, the incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Asynchronous forward bounding over a sequentially extended current partial assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize \(U=+\infty\) and extend a current partial assignment \(P\) according to the agent order. Whenever \(P\) changes, unassigned agents asynchronously return admissible estimates whose aggregate is \(B(P)\), a lower bound on the additional cost of completing \(P\). The assigning agent tests values and prunes a value once its accumulated cost plus the applicable forward estimates is at least \(U\). A complete assignment improving \(U\) is broadcast as the incumbent. Timestamps or assignment identifiers cause estimates for obsolete partial assignments to be ignored. Backtracking occurs when all values are exhausted, and termination follows when the root has exhausted every unpruned branch.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: AFB sequentially extends a partial assignment while unassigned agents asynchronously compute admissible future-cost bounds used for branch-and-bound pruning.
knowledge_statements.title: AFB Family

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is the correct role, but the forward-bound aggregation, value-pruning test, timestamp handling, backtracking, and root termination rules are defining AFB protocol details. No authoritative source with a locator is provided.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains and admissible lower bounds for every generated partial assignment.
Concurrent search contexts have unique identifiers, and messages are reliably delivered.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: If every branch is evaluated or admissibly pruned, the best shared incumbent is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Concurrent generalization of asynchronous forward-bounding branch-and-bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Initialize a shared incumbent \(U=+\infty\) and a finite collection \(\mathcal P\) of independently identified partial-assignment contexts. Agents concurrently extend contexts and request asynchronous forward estimates. For each \(P\in\mathcal P\), the combined quantity \(L(P)\) must lower-bound every completion of \(P\); the context is pruned when \(L(P)\geq U\). A completed context improving \(U\) broadcasts the new incumbent to all active searches. Context identifiers prevent bounds, assignments, or backtracks from one search being applied to another. The procedure terminates when every generated context has produced a complete assignment or has been validly pruned, and outputs the least-cost incumbent.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Concurrent forward bounding explores several identified partial assignments at once, sharing admissible bounds and the incumbent while isolating messages from different search contexts.
knowledge_statements.title: Concurrent Forward-Bounding Families

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits a concurrent forward-bounding family only at a generic level. The initialization of multiple contexts, allocation of branches, isolation of asynchronous messages, shared-incumbent semantics, and distributed termination are variant-specific and need a canonical reference.

assumptions_latex: The finite-domain DCOP is arranged as a rooted pseudo-tree, and every constraint joins ancestor-related variables.
Messages are reliably delivered, and local lower bounds are admissible.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the root satisfies its termination test, the selected assignments have globally minimum cost.

notation.meaning: lower bound maintained by agent i for value d
upper bound maintained by agent i for value d

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical asynchronous distributed optimization on a DCOP pseudo-tree.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Each agent \(i\) initializes, for every value \(d\), admissible bounds \(LB_i(d)\leq OPT_i(d)\leq UB_i(d)\) for its pseudo-tree subproblem and a threshold \(T_i\). It selects a value minimizing its current lower bound, sends VALUE and threshold information to children and lower-priority neighbors, and sends COST messages containing aggregated bounds to its parent. Received messages update the relevant contexts and bounds; inconsistent-context messages are discarded. Thresholds are allocated among children while preserving the parent's bound requirements. The root terminates when its global lower and upper bounds coincide, then propagates the value choices realizing the upper bound.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: ADOPT asynchronously exchanges value, cost-bound, and threshold messages on a pseudo-tree until the root's lower and upper bounds coincide at the global optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: ADOPT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Algorithm is appropriate for ADOPT, but the pseudo-tree assumptions, definitions and context dependence of the bounds, threshold allocation invariant, message recipients, termination test, and recovery of the optimizing assignments must be checked against the primary ADOPT specification.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finitely many variables and finite domains.
The constraint graph is organized by a rooted pseudo-tree, and communication is reliable.
All local costs are bounded below, with infeasible assignments represented by \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: When the root's incumbent upper bound equals its valid lower bound, the incumbent assignment is globally optimal; under the assumptions, this equality is reached after finitely many search expansions.

notation.meaning: Lower and upper bounds for value d under context X.
Current partial assignment along the pseudo-tree ancestors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite-domain minimization form of BnB-ADOPT with asynchronous pseudo-tree communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a minimization DCOP and a rooted pseudo-tree, BnB-ADOPT maintains for each agent \(i\), context \(X\), and value \(d\in D_i\) admissible bounds \(LB_i(d,X)\leq Q_i(d,X)\leq UB_i(d,X)\), where \(Q_i(d,X)\) is the best completion cost below \(i\). It explores values depth-first, propagates bound messages between pseudo-tree neighbors, updates \(U:=\min\{U,UB_i(d,X)\}\) when a better completion is found, and prunes a value whenever \(LB_i(d,X)\geq U\). The root stops when its aggregate lower bound equals its incumbent upper bound and returns the corresponding assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: BnB-ADOPT performs asynchronous depth-first branch-and-bound over a pseudo-tree, pruning values whose admissible lower bounds cannot improve the incumbent and terminating with an optimal assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: BnB-ADOPT

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No cited source supports the BnB-ADOPT-specific bound semantics, update rule, pruning rule, or finite-termination claim. The generic branch-and-bound sources in the inventory cannot establish this distributed protocol.

children.title: Weighted ADOPT Variants
children.top_down_role: ADOPT-family variants using weighting to alter search-quality behavior.

assumptions_latex: The underlying ADOPT bounds are valid for a finite-domain minimization DCOP.
A weight \(w\geq1\) is fixed.
Termination occurs only with a verifiable weighted lower-bound certificate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The returned assignment satisfies \(C(\widehat{x})\leq wC^*\) whenever costs are nonnegative and the certificate \(U\leq wL\) holds.

notation.meaning: Certified global lower bound and incumbent cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract multiplicative weighted-ADOPT scheme; published variants differ in where weights enter bound updates.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A weighted ADOPT variant accepts \(w\geq1\), runs asynchronous pseudo-tree search, and modifies value selection, pruning, or termination by comparing an incumbent upper bound \(U\) with a weighted admissible lower bound \(wL\). It preserves the unweighted feasibility semantics and outputs an incumbent \(\widehat{x}\) only after establishing \(U=C(\widehat{x})\leq wL\). Since admissibility gives \(L\leq C^*\), nonnegative costs imply \(C(\widehat{x})\leq wC^*\). At \(w=1\), the certificate reduces to exact optimality. The precise placement of \(w\) in local thresholds distinguishes individual weighted ADOPT variants.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Weighted ADOPT variants relax exact termination using a weight and return an incumbent whose cost is at most the weight times the optimum, subject to a valid certificate.
knowledge_statements.title: Weighted ADOPT Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record abstracts over materially different weighted ADOPT variants and supplies no source for where the weight enters the protocol or for the stated termination certificate. The elementary implication from U≤wL is sound, but it does not establish that a named variant maintains such a certificate.

children.title: Bounded ADOPT Variants
children.top_down_role: ADOPT-family variants organized around explicit solution-quality bounds.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP is a finite-domain minimization problem.
The algorithm maintains a feasible incumbent cost \(U\) and a valid global lower bound \(L\).
A nonnegative absolute tolerance \(\varepsilon\) or relative factor \(\rho\geq1\) is specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The absolute rule certifies \(C(\widehat{x})-C^*\leq\varepsilon\); for nonnegative costs, the relative rule certifies \(C(\widehat{x})\leq\rho C^*\).

notation.meaning: Certified lower bound and feasible incumbent cost.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Bounded termination expressed through global lower and upper certificates, independent of a particular message protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A bounded ADOPT variant may terminate with feasible assignment \(\widehat{x}\) of cost \(U=C(\widehat{x})\) when its distributed bounds establish either \(U-L\leq\varepsilon\) or \(U\leq\rho L\). Because \(L\leq C^*\leq U\), the absolute test yields \(C(\widehat{x})-C^*\leq U-L\leq\varepsilon\). If all relevant costs are nonnegative, the relative test yields \(C(\widehat{x})=U\leq\rho L\leq\rho C^*\). Bound messages must be combined without invalidating \(L\), and termination detection must confirm that the certificate refers to one consistent incumbent and bound state.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Bounded ADOPT may stop once distributed lower and upper bounds certify a requested absolute or multiplicative optimality gap for the current feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Bounded ADOPT Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The gap implications are mathematically valid given consistent global bounds, but no source shows that bounded ADOPT variants use these tests or can obtain the required consistent distributed state. The record currently describes generic certificates rather than a sourced algorithm family.

children.title: Weight–Bound Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Quality and resource implications associated with weighting or bounding choices.

assumptions_latex: A weighted ADOPT method returns only after certifying \(U\leq wL\).
The minimization costs and the optimal value are nonnegative.
Weights satisfy \(1\leq w_1\leq w_2\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The certified ratios obey \(C(\widehat{x}_{w_j})/C^*\leq w_j\); the admissible certificate set for \(w_1\) is contained in that for \(w_2\), but no monotonic runtime ordering follows.

notation.meaning: Feasible incumbent and certified lower bound.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical guarantee tradeoff only; search effort depends on instance and scheduling.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For \(1\leq w_1\leq w_2\), every pair \((L,U)\) satisfying \(U\leq w_1L\) also satisfies \(U\leq w_2L\). Thus increasing the weight weakens the required termination certificate and enlarges the set of incumbents that may be accepted. If \(L\leq C^*\) and costs are nonnegative, acceptance at weight \(w\) guarantees \(C(\widehat{x}_w)=U\leq wC^*\). This nesting does not imply that message count, computation, or wall-clock time is monotone in \(w\), because value ordering, asynchronous arrival, and incumbent discovery may change with the weight.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Larger weights weaken the certified quality guarantee and allow earlier acceptance, but they do not mathematically guarantee monotone reductions in messages, computation, or runtime.
knowledge_statements.title: Weight–Bound Tradeoffs

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Certificate nesting follows algebraically, but its interpretation as a weighted-ADOPT tradeoff and the nonmonotonic search-effort claim require a variant-specific source. Its prerequisite weighted and bounded variants are themselves unresolved.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains and additive local cost functions.
A rooted pseudo-tree covers the constraint graph.
Messages are delivered reliably.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The VALUE phase reconstructs an assignment \(x^*\) with \(C(x^*)=\min_x C(x)\); the largest tabular UTIL message is exponential in the induced separator width.

notation.meaning: Separator variables connecting i's subtree to its ancestors.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Classical tabular DPOP for finite-domain additive minimization DCOPs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
In the upward UTIL phase, each nonroot agent \(i\) receives child functions, adds them to its local functions, and eliminates its own variable by
\[U_i(x_{S_i})=\min_{x_i}\left(\sum_{f\in F_i}f(x_{\operatorname{scope}(f)})+\sum_{j\in\operatorname{ch}(i)}U_j(x_{S_j})\right).\]
It sends \(U_i\) to \(p(i)\). The root minimizes its aggregate and selects its value. In the downward VALUE phase, each agent receives the selected assignments of relevant separator variables, chooses a minimizing value retained from its UTIL computation, and sends the extended assignment to its children. The resulting joint assignment is globally optimal.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: DPOP eliminates variables upward through separator-indexed utility messages, then reconstructs a globally optimal assignment through downward value messages; tabular memory is exponential in induced width.
knowledge_statements.title: Classical DPOP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No DPOP source is cited. Moreover, the displayed recurrence does not define the allocation of local functions F_i precisely enough to ensure that every term depends only on x_i and its separator, and the induced-width memory conclusion needs a precise source and width convention.

assumptions_latex: The finite-domain DCOP and pseudo-tree satisfy the assumptions of classical DPOP.
Each stored utility table is restricted to at most \(M\) entries or an equivalent dimensional cap.
Residual separator dimensions are handled by exhaustive conditioning.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The method preserves exactness and completeness while bounding any stored table by \(M\), at the cost of repeated computation and potentially exponentially many conditioned subproblems.

notation.meaning: Remaining separator variables represented in a table.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact memory-bounded DPOP by conditioning oversized separators.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an agent \(i\) whose classical separator table exceeds \(M\), choose \(S_i=K_i\mathbin{\dot\cup}R_i\) so that a table over \(R_i\) fits the cap. Enumerate assignments \(a\in D_{K_i}\); for each \(a\), run the ordinary UTIL elimination with \(x_{K_i}=a\), store only the resulting function over \(R_i\), and combine the conditioned results by exact minimization. Retain compatible argmin information for the VALUE phase. Stop after every conditioning assignment has been processed and output the least-cost reconstructed assignment. No approximation is introduced, but subproblems may be recomputed.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Memory-bounded DPOP conditions on separator variables until each utility table fits a cap, preserving exactness while trading memory for repeated inference and enumeration.
knowledge_statements.title: Memory-Bounded DPOP

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed conditioning scheme is not tied to a named memory-bounded DPOP algorithm. No source establishes that it bounds every stored object by M while preserving exact VALUE reconstruction, nor that conditioned results can be combined as stated without exceeding the cap.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Solving Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems Using Logic Programming
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Solving Distributed Constraint Optimization Problems Using Logic Programming

children.title: Structured DPOP Variants
children.top_down_role: DPOP variants exploiting structured utility or constraint representations.

assumptions_latex: Each local cost and incoming message has an exact structured representation.
The representation supports exact addition, variable minimization, restriction, and comparison.
All intermediate scopes are finite.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Replacing tables by these exact structured objects leaves DPOP's computed separator functions and reconstructed optimum unchanged.

notation.meaning: Exact structured representation of function g.
Variables eliminated at one UTIL computation.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact representation-specialized DPOP, covering algebraic diagrams and other closed structured encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A structured DPOP variant replaces each tabular function \(g\) by an object \(\mathcal{R}(g)\) with exact semantics \(\llbracket\mathcal{R}(g)\rrbracket=g\). At agent \(i\), it computes
\[R_i=\operatorname{Min}_{E_i}\left(\operatorname{Add}(R_{i,1},\ldots,R_{i,k})\right),\]
where decoding commutes with the operations: \(\llbracket\operatorname{Add}(R_1,\ldots,R_k)\rrbracket=\sum_{ell=1}^k\llbracket R_ell\rrbracket\) and \(\llbracket\operatorname{Min}_{E}(R)\rrbracket=\min_{x_E}\llbracket R\rrbracket\). It sends \(R_i\) as its UTIL message and records exact argmin choices for VALUE reconstruction. The output equals classical DPOP's optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Structured DPOP performs DPOP's addition and elimination directly on exact compact function representations, preserving the classical optimum whenever the representation is closed under required operations.
knowledge_statements.title: Structured DPOP Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: This is a generic semantic lifting of DPOP rather than a sourced structured-DPOP variant. Exact addition and minimization are plausible sufficient ingredients, but scope management, witness recovery, and closure for actual intermediate objects require a concrete representation and citation.

children.title: Logic-Based DPOP Variants
children.top_down_role: DPOP variants using logic-oriented representations.

assumptions_latex: Finite-domain assignments are encoded by logical atoms.
Hard constraints and finite costs admit exact logical or weighted-logical representations.
The representation supports exact combination, forgetting, conditioning, and optimal-model extraction.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The decoded root optimum and the downward reconstructed assignment coincide with those of tabular DPOP.

notation.meaning: Logical encoding of a cost function g.
Exact minimization or forgetting of variables E.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Generic exact logic-based DPOP; concrete variants may use decision diagrams, clauses, or weighted formulas.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Encode every local function \(g\) by a weighted logical object \(\Phi_g\) whose model cost equals \(g\). Agent \(i\) combines local and child objects as \(\Phi_i=\bigotimes_{ell=1}^k\Phi_{i,ell}\), then eliminates its private variable by \(M_i=\exists^{\min}_{\{x_i\}}\Phi_i\). The operator must satisfy \(\operatorname{cost}_{M_i}(a)=\min_{d\in D_i}\operatorname{cost}_{\Phi_i}(a,d)\) for every separator assignment \(a\). The agent sends \(M_i\) upward and retains a minimizing witness. Downward conditioning on selected separator values recovers those witnesses and hence a globally optimal feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Logic-based DPOP encodes costs and constraints as weighted logical objects, combines them, eliminates variables by exact minimum-cost forgetting, and reconstructs an optimal model.
knowledge_statements.title: Logic-Based DPOP Variants

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No concrete weighted-logical formalism or logic-based DPOP source is identified. The meanings and availability of combination and minimum-cost forgetting vary by formalism, so the algorithm and optimality conclusion cannot be assessed reliably as written.

children.title: Representation Compatibility
children.top_down_role: Compatibility boundaries between DPOP variants and structured representation families.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains and additive costs.
Every encoded object has a total decoding map to an extended-real-valued function.
The DPOP pseudo-tree and separator scopes are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A representation is DPOP-compatible exactly when every intermediate UTIL function can be represented and all required operations preserve its decoded semantics.

notation.meaning: Decoding map from representations to functions.
Exact restriction to an assignment a.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Algebraic compatibility condition for exact representation-specialized DPOP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A representation class \(\mathscr{R}\) is compatible with exact DPOP if local functions are encodable in \(\mathscr{R}\), every intermediate separator function remains representable, and computable operations satisfy
\[\delta(R\widehat{+}S)=\delta(R)+\delta(S),\qquad \delta(\widehat{\min}_E R)=\min_{x_E}\delta(R),\qquad \delta(R\widehat{\mid}_a)=\delta(R)\mid_a.\]
It must also preserve extended costs such as \(+\infty\), identify scopes correctly, compare root values exactly, and recover a minimizing witness after conditioning. Closure without semantic equalities is insufficient, because approximation in any UTIL operation can change the optimum.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A representation is compatible with exact DPOP when it exactly encodes every intermediate function and is closed under addition, minimization, conditioning, comparison, and witness recovery.
knowledge_statements.title: Representation Compatibility

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The listed semantic-preservation requirements are plausible sufficient conditions, but the claim that compatibility holds 'exactly when' they hold is an unsupported necessity-and-sufficiency assertion. A sourced definition or theorem must specify required operations, representability, and witness reconstruction.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP cost is a sum of finite-scope functions over finite domains.
A rooted pseudo-tree assigns each local function to one agent bucket.
Each child UTIL message exactly summarizes its subtree.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The message \(U_i\) is exactly the minimum cost contributed by agent \(i\)'s subtree conditional on its separator assignment.

notation.meaning: Functions assigned to agent i's bucket.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact min-sum aggregation at one pseudo-tree bucket.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
For each nonroot agent \(i\), define its separator \(S_i\) as the ancestor variables adjacent to \(i\) or a descendant of \(i\). After receiving child summaries, agent \(i\) forms
\[G_i(x_i,x_{S_i})=\sum_{f\in B_i}f(x_{\operatorname{scope}(f)})+\sum_{j\in\operatorname{ch}(i)}U_j(x_{S_j}),\qquad U_i(x_{S_i})=\min_{x_i}G_i(x_i,x_{S_i}).\]
Assignments in each child separator are read consistently from \((x_i,x_{S_i})\). The function \(U_i\) is sent to the parent; a minimizing selector is retained for downward reconstruction.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An agent adds its local bucket functions to child subtree summaries and minimizes its own variable, producing an exact utility function indexed by its separator.
knowledge_statements.title: Separator Utility Aggregation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: No distributed bucket-elimination or DPOP source is supplied. The bucket rule must ensure that each local term and child message in G_i is evaluable from (x_i,x_{S_i}); merely assigning each function to an agent bucket does not state that invariant.

assumptions_latex: The target utility has finite scope and finite-domain arguments.
The encoding has exact evaluation semantics.
Combination and elimination are performed without approximation.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The compact object may replace a table in distributed bucket elimination without changing any separator utility or optimal assignment.

notation.meaning: Compact encoding of utility function u.
Decoded value of representation R at assignment a.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semantic requirement for compact exact UTIL-message encodings.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
A compact utility representation of \(u:D_S\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\}\) is an object \(R_u\) satisfying \(\delta(R_u)(a)=u(a)\) for every \(a\in D_S\), with encoded size \(|R_u|\) potentially smaller than \(|D_S|\). For exact distributed elimination, the class must provide semantics-preserving encoded addition and minimization:
\[\delta(R_u\widehat{+}R_v)=u+v,\qquad \delta(\widehat{\min}_E R_u)=\min_{x_E}u.\]
It must additionally support conditioning and recovery of a minimizing value. Compactness is instance-dependent; no representation is required to be smaller than a table for every utility function.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compact utility object exactly represents a separator function and supports exact addition, elimination, conditioning, and argmin recovery; compression is instance-dependent rather than universal.
knowledge_statements.title: Compact Utility Representations

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The exact-decoding definition is coherent, but no source supports it as the intended compact-utility framework. Exact replacement in DPOP additionally depends on scope handling, representability of every intermediate result, exact comparisons, and compatible witness reconstruction, which are not formalized here.

children.title: OptAPO
children.top_down_role: The OptAPO branch of partially centralized DCOP resolution.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains and additive costs.
Agents communicate reliably and mediation sessions use consistent conflict resolution.
Every unresolved conflict eventually enters a mediation scope whose centralized subproblem is solved exactly.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Under these fairness and coverage assumptions, termination yields a globally optimal assignment; without them, partial overlays can stabilize prematurely or livelock.

notation.meaning: Current mediation scope of mediator i.

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract optimal partial-overlay mediation scheme; protocol-specific completeness invariants require a primary source.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: OptAPO maintains overlapping agent views and dynamically elects mediators. A mediator \(i\) collects the current assignments and relevant constraints for \(G_i\), solves the induced subproblem exactly while accounting for constraints crossing its boundary, and proposes a jointly consistent reassignment that lowers the best known feasible cost or proves no improvement within that scope. Agents accept nonconflicting sessions, update their views, and enlarge future mediation scopes when external conflicts remain. The process stops only when distributed termination detection establishes feasibility and that no omitted conflict or improving scope remains; it then outputs the incumbent \(x\). Global optimality depends on eventual scope coverage and exact mediation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: OptAPO repeatedly centralizes dynamically chosen overlapping subproblems, solves them exactly, propagates assignments, and expands mediation scopes until distributed termination certifies a global optimum.
knowledge_statements.title: OptAPO

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: OptAPO's mediation, locking, scope-growth, termination, and completeness conditions are protocol-specific and cannot be reconstructed from generic fairness and coverage assumptions. A primary source is required to determine whether this description and global-optimality claim match OptAPO rather than an abstract overlay method.

children.title: Partial-Overlay Methods
children.top_down_role: Methods coordinating through temporary or limited centralized overlays.

assumptions_latex: A finite DCOP has variables \(x_i\in D_i\) and objective \(F(x)=\sum_{f\in\mathcal F}f(x_{\operatorname{scp}(f)})\).
Each agent controls one variable and communicates reliably with agents sharing a constraint.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Each completed mediation replaces the current values on \(S_m\) by a minimizer of the mediator's induced subproblem, conditional on its current boundary view.

notation.meaning: Variables included in mediator m's current overlay
Overlay boundary variables outside the mediated set

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Abstract algorithmic form of partial-overlay mediation, without committing to a particular APO protocol variant.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given a conflicted mediator \(m\), construct an overlay \(S_m\) containing \(m\) and selected constraint-neighbors. Obtain a consistent snapshot of assignments on \(S_m\cup\partial S_m\), and compute \[y_{S_m}\in\operatorname*{argmin}_{z_{S_m}\in\prod_{i\in S_m}D_i}\sum_{f:\,\operatorname{scp}(f)\cap S_m\ne\varnothing}f\bigl(z_{S_m},x_{\partial S_m}\bigr).\] If the mediation protocol's locking and acceptance conditions hold, atomically replace \(x_{S_m}\) by \(y_{S_m}\); otherwise release the participants and retry after updating the overlay view. Terminate only under the chosen quiescence rule, and output the latest globally assembled assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A mediator temporarily centralizes an overlapping subproblem, optimizes its variables against the observed boundary assignment, and commits the joint update only when the protocol's consistency conditions hold.
knowledge_statements.title: Partial-Overlay Methods

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The algorithmic role fits the leaf, but no DCOP/APO source is cited. The locking, acceptance, retry, quiescence, and overlay-construction rules are protocol-dependent, and the displayed objective does not formally define how each factor receives variables outside the overlay. A specific primary-source locator is required before the mathematical version can be assessed reliably.

children.title: Overlay-Mediation Boundaries
