children.title: Critical-Path Tradeoffs
children.top_down_role: Relationships between exploitable concurrency and end-to-end latency.

knowledge_statements.title: Critical-Path Tradeoffs
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Relates work, dependency span, processor count, and achievable execution latency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let an execution consist of unit-time tasks forming a finite acyclic dependency graph, with total work \(W\) and critical-path length \(S\). Every schedule on \(P\ge1\) identical processors has makespan \(T_P\) satisfying \[T_P\ge\max\left\{\frac{W}{P},S\right\}.\] A greedy list schedule that runs any available task whenever a processor is idle satisfies \[T_P\le\frac{W}{P}+S.\] Consequently, increasing \(P\) can reduce the work-limited term but cannot lower latency below the critical path; useful parallelism is bounded on the order of \(W/S\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: P processors cannot beat either work divided by P or the critical path; greedy scheduling achieves their sum up to rounding.
assumptions_latex: \text{the task graph is finite and acyclic}
\text{every task has unit processing time}
P\ge1\text{ identical processors are available}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \max\{W/P,S\}\le T_P\le W/P+S
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The work/span lower bound and stated greedy upper bound fit this complexity-bound leaf, but the scheduling theorem and its precise assumptions require an authoritative citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Completeness–Scalability Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: States the worst-case scalability boundary for complete finite-domain DCOP optimization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider finite-domain DCOPs represented extensionally, and require an algorithm to terminate with a globally optimal assignment or a correct infeasibility declaration on every instance. This complete task contains finite constraint optimization as a special case and is NP-hard. Hence, unless \(\mathrm{P}=\mathrm{NP}\), no complete algorithm has worst-case running time polynomial in the full extensional input length for all such instances. Completeness therefore permits exponential worst-case resource growth; polynomial scaling can be guaranteed only after restricting the instance class, structural parameters, or required quality guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Global completeness for unrestricted finite-domain DCOPs is NP-hard, so polynomial worst-case scaling requires structural restrictions or a relaxed guarantee unless P equals NP.
assumptions_latex: \text{finite-domain cost functions are represented extensionally}
\text{the algorithm must solve every input to global optimality}
\mathrm{P}\ne\mathrm{NP}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \text{no complete algorithm has worst-case running time polynomial in the input length on all instances}
review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The failure-boundary role fits the tradeoff leaf, but the NP-hardness claim and its reduction from finite constraint optimization are uncited.

knowledge_statements.title: Memory–Communication Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Quantifies message fragmentation forced by a bounded communication buffer.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Suppose an agent must transmit a table containing \(N\) independently encoded entries to another agent, losslessly and without recomputation at the receiver. If at most \(B\ge1\) entries may be buffered in one outgoing message, then every transmission scheme uses at least \[K\ge\left\lceil\frac{N}{B}\right\rceil\] messages. Partitioning the table into consecutive blocks of at most \(B\) entries attains equality. Thus lowering the sender's message-buffer capacity from \(N\) to \(B\) preserves the transmitted entry volume but can increase message count to \(\lceil N/B\rceil\), excluding headers and acknowledgments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Sending N table entries with capacity B entries per message requires at least ceiling N over B messages, and simple block partitioning attains this bound.
assumptions_latex: N\ge1\text{ entries must be transmitted losslessly}
1\le B\le N\text{ entries fit in each outgoing message}
\text{receiver-side recomputation is excluded}
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: K_{\min}=\left\lceil N/B\right\rceil

notation.meaning: Number of table entries to transmit

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The fragmentation bound is correct under its model and complexity_bound is suitable, but it captures only a narrow buffer-versus-message-count tradeoff and lacks a source establishing that model for this DCOP leaf.

knowledge_statements.title: Width–Depth Ordering Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formulates pseudo-tree selection as a biobjective width–depth optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal T(G)\) be the finite set of rooted pseudo-trees of a primal graph \(G\). For \(T\in\mathcal T(G)\), let \(w(T)\) be its induced width under the associated elimination order and let \(h(T)\) be its root-to-leaf depth. The width–depth tradeoff is represented by the attainable set \[\mathcal A(G)=\{(w(T),h(T)):T\in\mathcal T(G)\}\] and its Pareto frontier \[\mathcal P(G)=\{(w,h)\in\mathcal A(G):\nexists(w',h')\in\mathcal A(G),\ w'\le w,\ h'\le h,\ (w',h')\ne(w,h)\}.\] Selecting an ordering requires choosing a point on this frontier when no single pseudo-tree minimizes both coordinates.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Each pseudo-tree yields induced width and depth. Nondominated pairs form the Pareto frontier from which an algorithm-specific ordering is selected.
assumptions_latex: G\text{ is a finite connected primal graph}
\mathcal T(G)\ne\varnothing
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \mathcal P(G)=\operatorname{Min}_{\le_{\mathrm{prod}}}\mathcal A(G)

notation.meaning: Induced width associated with pseudo-tree T
Pareto frontier of attainable width-depth pairs

review_flags: auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Pareto-set representation fits the tradeoff leaf, but the mapping from a pseudo-tree to its associated elimination order and induced width is convention-dependent and unsupported by a citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralization–Distribution Tradeoff
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Point-to-point comparison of coordinator-based and distributed DCOP execution.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(H=(A,F)\) be a connected communication graph with \(|A|=n\), and let every agent's private input affect the required global solution. Any execution that centralizes all inputs at one coordinator must use at least \(n-1\) message transmissions before solving. If every agent must subsequently receive a coordinator-derived decision, dissemination requires at least another \(n-1\) transmissions. A spanning-tree implementation attains these bounds with \(2(n-1)\) transmissions, at most twice the tree depth in synchronous rounds, and coordinator storage equal to the aggregate input size. Avoiding that storage and disclosure distributes computation but generally retains coordination communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A coordinator can simplify global computation, but collecting all necessary inputs and returning decisions costs at least two spanning-tree traversals and concentrates storage and disclosure.
assumptions_latex: \(H\) is connected and communication is point-to-point.
Every agent's input can change the required solution.
Every agent must receive its coordinator-derived decision.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathrm{collect}}\ge n-1\), \(M_{\mathrm{return}}\ge n-1\), and a spanning tree attains \(M_{\mathrm{total}}=2(n-1)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle fits the tradeoff container, but the exact collection and dissemination lower bounds depend on a formal information-distribution and message-accounting model. No cited source supports those hypotheses or the claimed tightness, so the record requires an inspectable distributed-computing or DCOP source.

knowledge_statements.title: Neighbor-Only Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Communication restricted to adjacency in the DCOP interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(A,E)\) be the primal interaction graph of a DCOP, where \(\{i,j\}\in E\) exactly when agents \(i\) and \(j\) own variables occurring together in a constraint. A protocol uses neighbor-only communication when every point-to-point message sent from \(i\) to \(j\) satisfies \(\{i,j\}\in E\). Information for a nonneighbor may therefore be conveyed only through a sequence of neighbor transmissions along a path in \(G\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents may send directly only to agents sharing a constraint; information for other agents must be relayed along interaction-graph paths.
assumptions_latex: Each controlled variable has a designated owning agent.
Messages have identifiable sender and receiver.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(E_{\mathrm{msg}}\subseteq E\).

notation.meaning: set of ordered-message endpoint pairs, viewed without orientation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is mathematically coherent and fits the communication-model leaf, but it identifies DCOP neighbors specifically with primal interaction-graph adjacency without citing a source establishing that convention.

children.title: Nonlocal Communication
children.top_down_role: Communication regimes permitting contact beyond immediate problem-graph neighbors.

knowledge_statements.title: Nonlocal Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct messaging beyond DCOP interaction-graph adjacency.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(A,E)\) be the DCOP interaction graph and \(H=(A,F)\) the graph of permitted direct communication channels. Communication is nonlocal relative to \(G\) when \(F\nsubseteq E\); equivalently, some agents that share no constraint may exchange a direct message. The nonlocal channels are precisely \(F\setminus E\). This classification concerns logical endpoints: a direct logical channel may itself be implemented by multiple transmissions in an underlying physical network.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Communication is nonlocal when at least one direct logical channel joins agents that do not share a DCOP constraint.
assumptions_latex: The interaction and communication graphs have the same agent set.
Directness refers to logical message endpoints.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(F\nsubseteq E\), with nonlocal channel set \(F\setminus E\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and distinguishes logical from physical directness, but that convention and the graph-based characterization have no supporting citation. The supplied local inventory does not address distributed communication models.

children.title: Overlay Communication
children.top_down_role: Communication organized through a logical overlay distinct from the base problem graph.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlay Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Logical communication channels routed through a physical network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(P=(U,L)\) be a physical network containing agent locations and let \(O=(A,F)\) be a logical communication graph. An overlay implementation assigns every logical edge \(e=\{i,j\}\in F\) a physical path \(\rho(e)\) in \(P\) joining the locations of \(i\) and \(j\). Sending one logical message on \(e\) induces transmissions along \(\rho(e)\); hence logical message count, physical transmission count, and latency need not coincide.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An overlay exposes logical agent-to-agent channels, each implemented by a path through the underlying physical network.
assumptions_latex: Every overlay endpoint has a location in the physical network.
Each overlay edge is assigned a realizable physical path.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\rho:F\to\{\text{physical paths in }P\}\), with \(\partial\rho(\{i,j\})=\{i,j\}\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is internally consistent and appropriate for overlay communication, but no distributed-systems source is cited for the routing-map model or the distinction among logical messages, physical transmissions, and latency.

children.title: Overlay Reachability Regimes
children.top_down_role: Structural limits on agent reachability through logical communication overlays.

knowledge_statements.title: Overlay Reachability Regimes
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Reachability classifications induced by an overlay graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an overlay graph \(O=(A,F)\), write \(d_O(i,j)\) for shortest-path distance, with value \(\infty\) when no path exists. The overlay has full reachability when \(d_O(i,j)<\infty\) for every pair; component-limited reachability when this holds exactly within connected components; and \(k\)-bounded reachability when every reachable pair satisfies \(d_O(i,j)\le k\). Under store-and-forward communication, these regimes respectively permit global, componentwise, or bounded-hop information propagation.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Overlay reachability may be global, confined to connected components, or bounded by a maximum logical hop count.
assumptions_latex: The overlay is a static undirected graph during the considered execution.
Messages may be forwarded along overlay paths.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\max_{i,j\in A}d_O(i,j)<\infty\) characterizes full reachability; \(d_O(i,j)\le k\) for every reachable pair characterizes the \(k\)-bounded regime.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: A source is needed to determine the intended reachability taxonomy. As written, component-limited reachability is true of every undirected graph, while full reachability and k-bounded reachability can overlap, so the claimed list does not yet define a reliable set of regimes.

knowledge_statements.title: Mediated Communication
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Agent communication routed through designated intermediary processes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the optimizing agents and \(M\) a disjoint set of mediators. Communication is mediated when every logical exchange from one agent \(i\) to another agent \(j\) is implemented by a path whose internal vertices include at least one member of \(M\). A single-mediator star is the special case in which some \(m\in M\) receives every agent message and sends every inter-agent response, so no inter-agent exchange is direct.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents communicate through designated intermediary processes; in a mediator star, every inter-agent exchange passes through one mediator.
assumptions_latex: \(A\cap M=\varnothing\).
Communication paths identify their internal relay processes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(i\leadsto j\) implies that the implementing path has an internal vertex in \(M\).

notation.meaning: logical exchange from agent i to agent j

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record gives a precise strict-mediation model, but the title could also cover systems in which only selected exchanges are mediated. No source establishes that every inter-agent exchange must contain a mediator as an internal vertex.

assumptions_latex: The recipient set is fixed when the broadcast is issued.
The communication layer preserves payload identity.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{deliver}(i,m,R)=\{(j,m):j\in R\}\).
knowledge_statements.scope_note: One-to-many delivery under an explicit broadcast cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A\) be the agents. A broadcast event by sender \(i\in A\) with payload \(m\) and recipient set \(R\subseteq A\setminus\{i\}\) requests delivery of the same payload to every member of \(R\). Under logical-broadcast accounting it counts as one message event; under point-to-point accounting it induces \(|R|\) deliveries, plus any forwarding transmissions required by the network. Correct receipt requires each intended recipient to obtain an identical copy of \(m\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A sender transmits one payload to a recipient set; its cost is one logical broadcast or multiple physical deliveries, depending on accounting.
knowledge_statements.title: Broadcast Communication
Synchronous Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Round-based coordination with bounded, ordered phase progression.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed execution is synchronous when it is partitioned into rounds \(r=0,1,2,\ldots\), and each agent's round-\(r\) action is computed from its initial state and messages delivered by the start of that round. Every message sent during round \(r\) is delivered by the start of round \(r+1\), and no agent begins round \(r+1\) before completing round \(r\). Thus the round number provides a common logical time for coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agents progress through common logical rounds, and every message sent in one round arrives before the next round begins.
assumptions_latex: Agents and channels do not fail during the execution.
The model supplies a common round discipline.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{sendround}(m)=r\) implies \(\operatorname{deliverround}(m)\le r+1\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the synchronous-coordination leaf, but it selects a particular round-delivery convention and failure-free model without an authoritative distributed-algorithms citation.

knowledge_statements.title: Asynchronous Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination without global rounds or known timing bounds.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A distributed execution is asynchronous when process steps and message deliveries are ordered only by local causality, with no global round structure and no known finite upper bound on relative process speed or message delay. A fair reliable execution additionally requires every continuously enabled nonfailed agent eventually to take a step and every sent message eventually to be delivered. Algorithms must therefore preserve correctness under every event ordering satisfying causality and these fairness conditions.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: There are no global rounds or known delay bounds; correctness must tolerate every causal ordering, while fairness ensures eventual steps and delivery.
assumptions_latex: Channels are reliable but may delay messages arbitrarily.
Agents do not fail in the execution considered.
Fairness applies to enabled agents and sent messages.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname{send}(m)\prec\operatorname{deliver}(m)\), while no uniform finite delivery bound is assumed.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition is coherent for a failure-free fair asynchronous model, but fairness, reliability, and the absence of timing bounds are model choices requiring an authoritative source and specific locator.

knowledge_statements.title: Partially Synchronous Coordination
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Eventual-bounded-delay model between synchronous and asynchronous coordination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An execution is partially synchronous in the eventual-bounds sense when there exist finite constants \(T\), \(\Delta\), and \(\Phi\), unknown to the agents, such that after time \(T\), every message is delivered within \(\Delta\) time units and every nonfailed agent takes at least one step in each interval of length \(\Phi\). Before \(T\), delays and relative process speeds may be unbounded. Coordination may exploit the bounds only through observations such as expiring timeouts.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Timing may initially be arbitrary, but after an unknown stabilization time, message delays and process-step intervals satisfy fixed finite bounds.
assumptions_latex: A real-time ordering exists for specification purposes.
Agents and reliable channels remain nonfailed after stabilization.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(t\ge T\) implies \(d_{\mathrm{msg}}(t)\le\Delta\) and \(d_{\mathrm{step}}(t)\le\Phi\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement selects an eventual-bounds form of partial synchrony with unknown stabilization time and unknown delay and process bounds. Partial synchrony has several non-equivalent standard variants, so an authoritative source is needed to validate this exact version.

assumptions_latex: Instance size and admissible executions are specified.
A message-counting convention is fixed.
All considered executions terminate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M_{\mathcal A}(n)=\sup_{|I|=n}\sup_{e\in\mathcal E(I)}N_{\mathrm{msg}}(\mathcal A,I,e)\).

notation.meaning: number of counted sends before output

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the worst-case number of logical messages before termination.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a distributed algorithm \(\mathcal A\), instance-size parameter \(n\), and admissible execution set \(\mathcal E(I)\), define its worst-case message-count complexity by \[M_{\mathcal A}(n)=\sup_{I:\,|I|=n}\ \sup_{e\in\mathcal E(I)} N_{\mathrm{msg}}(\mathcal A,I,e).\] Here each point-to-point send counts once; a broadcast counts according to a separately declared convention. Only messages sent before all required outputs are produced are counted. The assertion \(M_{\mathcal A}(n)=O(f(n))\) means that constants \(c,n_0>0\) satisfy \(M_{\mathcal A}(n)\le c f(n)\) for all \(n\ge n_0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message-count complexity is the worst-case number of counted sends before all outputs appear, maximized over equal-size instances and admissible executions.
knowledge_statements.title: Message-Count Complexity

assumptions_latex: A uniquely decodable binary encoding is fixed.
Instance size and admissible executions are specified.
All considered executions terminate.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(S_{\mathcal A}(n)=\sup_{|I|=n}\sup_{e\in\mathcal E(I)}\sup\bigl(\{|\operatorname{enc}(m)|:m\in\operatorname{Msg}(\mathcal A,I,e)\}\cup\{0\}\bigr)\).

notation.meaning: worst-case maximum message length in bits

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Definition of the worst-case encoded length of an individual transmitted message.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a binary, uniquely decodable encoding of messages. For distributed algorithm \(\mathcal A\), define the worst-case message-size complexity at instance size \(n\) by \[S_{\mathcal A}(n)=\sup_{I:\,|I|=n}\ \sup_{e\in\mathcal E(I)}\ \sup\bigl(\{|\operatorname{enc}(m)|:m\in\operatorname{Msg}(\mathcal A,I,e)\}\cup\{0\}\bigr).\] The bound concerns the largest individual payload sent before termination, including prescribed headers but excluding lower-layer framing unless declared otherwise. The assertion \(S_{\mathcal A}(n)=O(f(n))\) uses the usual eventual constant-factor convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Message-size complexity is the maximum encoded bit length of any single message over equal-size instances and admissible executions, with value zero for an execution that sends no messages.
knowledge_statements.title: Message-Size Complexity
Communication-Round Complexity
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Worst-case synchronous round complexity for a distributed constraint-optimization protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Pi\) be a synchronous distributed protocol, let \(\mathcal I_n\) be its admissible DCOP instances of size \(n\), and let \(\Sigma(I)\) be the permitted executions on instance \(I\). For an execution \(\sigma\), define \(R_\Pi(I,\sigma)\) as the number of communication rounds through the round containing its last message; a round permits local computation followed by message transmission to neighbors. The communication-round complexity is \[\mathsf{RC}_\Pi(n)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I_n}\sup_{\sigma\in\Sigma(I)}R_\Pi(I,\sigma).\] If every admissible execution terminates without communication, its round count is \(0\); if some admissible execution does not terminate, the complexity is \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Round complexity is the worst-case number of synchronous communication rounds through the final message, over admissible instances and executions of the protocol.
assumptions_latex: \(\Pi\) operates in a synchronous round model.
The instance-size parameter \(n\) and admissible execution set \(\Sigma(I)\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{RC}_\Pi(n)=\sup_{I\in\mathcal I_n,\,\sigma\in\Sigma(I)}R_\Pi(I,\sigma)\).

notation.meaning: communication rounds used by an execution

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition fits the leaf and is internally coherent, but no cited source supports the chosen synchronous-round convention, treatment of the last-message round, or assignment of infinite complexity to nonterminating executions.

children.title: Routing Cost
children.top_down_role: Communication costs attributable to message routing across network paths.

knowledge_statements.title: Routing Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hop- and bandwidth-sensitive cost of realizing logical DCOP messages on a physical network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a communication graph. Each logical message \(m\) has size \(b_m\ge 0\) and is routed along a path \(P_m\subseteq E\). Given nonnegative per-edge transmission weights \(w_e\), its routing cost and the execution's total routing cost are \[\mathsf{route}(m)=b_m\sum_{e\in P_m}w_e,\qquad \mathsf{Route}(\sigma)=\sum_{m\in M(\sigma)}\mathsf{route}(m).\] With \(w_e=1\), this counts bit-hops; with \(b_m=1\), it counts weighted message-hops. Repeated traversals are counted with multiplicity.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Routing cost sums message size times the weighted length of each physical route, counting every edge traversal.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the physical communication graph.
Every transmitted logical message has a specified route and nonnegative size.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Route}(\sigma)=\sum_{m\in M(\sigma)}b_m\sum_{e\in P_m}w_e\).

notation.meaning: physical route of logical message m
cost per transmitted unit on edge e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits Routing Cost, but the bit-hop/weighted-hop functional is a selected convention without a supporting network or DCOP source. The supplied inventory does not substantiate it.

children.title: Locality Cost
children.top_down_role: Communication costs attributable to the placement of interacting agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Locality Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Maximum communication radius of a DCOP execution in the physical network.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(G=(V,E)\) be a connected communication graph with shortest-path distance \(d_G\). For an execution \(\sigma\), let \(M(\sigma)\) contain its logical messages, and let \(s(m),t(m)\in V\) be the originating and destination agents of message \(m\). The locality cost is \[\mathsf{Loc}(\sigma)=\max_{m\in M(\sigma)}d_G\bigl(s(m),t(m)\bigr),\] with \(\mathsf{Loc}(\sigma)=0\) when no message is sent. Thus locality measures the farthest logical dependency exercised by communication, independently of how many messages traverse that distance.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Locality cost is the largest network distance between the originating and destination agents of any logical message.
assumptions_latex: \(G\) is connected and its shortest-path distance is defined.
Each logical message has identified originating and destination agents.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Loc}(\sigma)=\max_{m\in M(\sigma)}d_G(s(m),t(m))\), with empty maximum defined as \(0\).

notation.meaning: shortest-path distance in the communication graph
logical messages sent during execution sigma

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Locality has multiple established meanings. No citation supports defining it specifically as the maximum source-to-destination graph distance of a logical message rather than route radius, communication dilation, or another locality measure.

children.title: Topology-Sensitive Communication Cost
children.top_down_role: Cost variation induced by physical or logical network topology.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology-Sensitive Communication Cost
knowledge_statements.scope_note: General edge-load functional retaining the physical location of communication.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For an execution \(\sigma\) on \(G=(V,E)\), let \(x_e(\sigma)\ge 0\) be the total transmitted volume across edge \(e\), counting repeated traversals, and let \(c_e:[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty]\) be a nondecreasing edge-cost function with \(c_e(0)=0\). Its topology-sensitive communication cost is \[\mathsf{TC}_G(\sigma)=\sum_{e\in E}c_e\bigl(x_e(\sigma)\bigr).\] Linear choices \(c_e(x)=w_ex\) recover weighted routing volume, while nonlinear choices can model congestion or scarce links. Unlike message count alone, this functional distinguishes executions inducing different edge-load vectors.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topology-sensitive cost applies edge-specific cost functions to transmitted loads and sums them, thereby retaining where communication occurs.
assumptions_latex: \(G=(V,E)\) is the physical communication graph.
Each \(c_e\) is nonnegative, nondecreasing, and satisfies \(c_e(0)=0\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{TC}_G(\sigma)=\sum_{e\in E}c_e(x_e(\sigma))\).

notation.meaning: communication volume carried by edge e

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The edge-load functional is mathematically coherent and topology-sensitive, but it is a broad constructed cost family rather than a sourced standard definition for this DCOP leaf. Its aggregation and congestion interpretation require evidence.

children.title: Agent Privacy
children.top_down_role: Protection of information concerning participating agents.

knowledge_statements.title: Agent Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of hidden agent participation or ownership attributes from an observer's protocol view.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix an observer coalition \(O\), a protocol \(\Pi\), and a public-information map \(p\). Let \(a(I)\) encode the secret agent-level data of instance \(I\), such as participation or variable ownership, and let \(V_O^\Pi(I)\) be the coalition's random view. The protocol provides perfect agent privacy relative to an admissible relation \(\sim_a\) if, for every \(I\sim_a I'\) satisfying \(p(I)=p(I')\) but possibly \(a(I)\ne a(I')\), \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\] The view includes the coalition's inputs, randomness, received messages, and prescribed outputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Agent privacy holds when admissible changes to hidden participation or ownership data do not change an observer coalition's view distribution.
assumptions_latex: The observer coalition and its complete protocol view are specified.
The relation \(\sim_a\) identifies admissible changes to secret agent-level data.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\sim_a I'\) and \(p(I)=p(I')\) imply \(V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I')\).

notation.meaning: random view of observer coalition O

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The indistinguishability template is coherent, but no DCOP privacy source establishes that Agent Privacy jointly covers hidden participation and variable ownership or that perfect distributional indistinguishability is the intended notion.

children.title: Identity Privacy
children.top_down_role: Protection of identifying information associated with participants.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of real-agent assignments to protocol-visible pseudonyms or roles.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a protocol \(\Pi\), observer coalition \(O\), public-information map \(p\), and a set of visible protocol labels \(L\). For instance \(I\), let \(\iota_I:L\to A\) assign each visible label to its real agent. Perfect identity privacy holds relative to admissible relabelings if, whenever instances \(I,I'\) have \(p(I)=p(I')\) and differ only through an admissible change from \(\iota_I\) to \(\iota_{I'}\), \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\] Thus the observer's transcript cannot distinguish which real agent occupies a hidden visible role beyond public information.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity privacy makes admissible assignments of visible protocol labels to real agents indistinguishable to the observer.
assumptions_latex: Visible labels and the real-agent identity space are specified.
Admissible identity relabelings preserve all declared public information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(p(I)=p(I')\) and admissible \(\iota_I\mapsto\iota_{I'}\) imply \(V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I')\).

notation.meaning: mapping from visible labels to real agents

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The label-to-real-agent formulation fits the title in one possible model, but identity privacy has model-dependent meanings. A source is needed for the visible-label mapping and perfect-indistinguishability definition.

children.title: Identity-Linkage Leakage
children.top_down_role: Leakage arising from linking pseudonyms, roles, messages, or assignments to identities.

knowledge_statements.title: Identity-Linkage Leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information revealed about the mapping between visible protocol labels and real agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\Iota\) be a random hidden mapping from visible protocol labels to real agents, let \(P\) denote public information, and let \(V_O\) be an observer coalition's random protocol view. Identity-linkage leakage is the conditional mutual information \[\mathsf{Leak}_{\mathrm{id}}(O)=I(\Iota;V_O\mid P).\] It is zero exactly when \(\Iota\) and \(V_O\) are conditionally independent given \(P\). The definition measures disclosure of label-to-identity linkage, rather than disclosure already implied by public information; logarithm base two gives leakage in bits.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identity-linkage leakage is the conditional mutual information between the hidden label-to-agent mapping and an observer's view, given public information.
assumptions_latex: \(\Iota\), \(P\), and \(V_O\) have a joint distribution.
The relevant conditional mutual information is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Leak}_{\mathrm{id}}(O)=I(\Iota;V_O\mid P)\), and it vanishes iff \(\Iota\perp V_O\mid P\).

notation.meaning: random view of observer coalition O

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: Conditional mutual information is mathematically well-defined under the stated assumptions, but no source establishes it as the intended identity-linkage leakage metric in DCOPs rather than one optional quantitative formalization.

knowledge_statements.title: Topology Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of admissible hidden changes to the DCOP interaction graph.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a DCOP instance \(I\), let \(H(I)\) be its secret constraint or interaction graph, let \(p(I)\) be public information, and let \(V_O^\Pi(I)\) be observer coalition \(O\)'s random view under protocol \(\Pi\). Perfect topology privacy relative to an admissible topology relation \(\sim_H\) holds if every pair \(I\sim_H I'\) with \(p(I)=p(I')\) satisfies \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\] The admissibility relation must preserve the declared outputs and any topology information intentionally exposed to \(O\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Topology privacy holds when admissible hidden changes to the DCOP interaction graph leave an observer coalition's view distribution unchanged.
assumptions_latex: The secret graph and publicly exposed topology information are separated.
The relation \(\sim_H\) specifies output-preserving admissible topology changes.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\sim_H I'\) and \(p(I)=p(I')\) imply \(V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I')\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The statement is coherent, but topology privacy may concern the constraint graph, communication graph, agent graph, or their relationships. No DCOP-specific source supports the selected interaction-graph and perfect-indistinguishability formulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Internal Constraint Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of constraints whose entire scope is owned by one nonobserving agent.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(o:X\to A\) assign DCOP variables to agents. A constraint \(f_S\) with scope \(S\subseteq X\) is internal to agent \(a\) when \(o(x)=a\) for every \(x\in S\). Fix an observer coalition \(O\) not containing \(a\). Protocol \(\Pi\) provides perfect internal-constraint privacy if any admissible instances \(I,I'\) differing only in the existence, scope, or table of constraints internal to \(a\), while preserving public information and prescribed outputs, satisfy \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\]
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Internal constraint privacy hides admissible changes to constraints involving only variables owned by one unobserved agent.
assumptions_latex: Every variable has a designated owning agent.
Compared internal-constraint changes preserve public information and prescribed outputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible changes confined to constraints internal to \(a\notin O\) leave \(V_O^\Pi\) unchanged in distribution.

notation.meaning: constraint or cost function with scope S

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The ownership-based internal-scope definition is plausible, but the privacy claim blends constraint existence, scope, and table values. A DCOP source is required to establish this boundary and the selected perfect-indistinguishability semantics.

knowledge_statements.title: External Constraint Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of constraints whose scopes cross agent-ownership boundaries.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(o:X\to A\) assign variables to agents. A constraint \(f_S\) is external when its scope satisfies \(\lvert\{o(x):x\in S\}\rvert\ge 2\). For observer coalition \(O\), protocol \(\Pi\) provides perfect external-constraint privacy if every admissible pair \(I,I'\) that agrees on public information and prescribed outputs, and differs only in secret existence, scope, or incidence data of external constraints not authorized to \(O\), satisfies \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\] Values of exposed constraint tables are outside this structural definition unless separately declared secret.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: External constraint privacy hides admissible structural changes to constraints spanning variables owned by multiple agents.
assumptions_latex: Every variable has a designated owning agent.
Compared instances preserve public information and prescribed outputs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Admissible secret changes to external-constraint structure leave \(V_O^\Pi\) unchanged in distribution.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The cross-owner scope criterion is plausible, but no source supports restricting External Constraint Privacy to existence, scope, and incidence while excluding valuations. The chosen privacy semantics are also unsourced.

children.title: Valuation Privacy
children.top_down_role: Protection of utility, cost, or preference information associated with DCOP evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Valuation Privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Indistinguishability of secret numerical constraint values under admissible value-table changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a DCOP instance \(I	empeq\), let \(F(I)=(f_S)_{S\in\mathcal S}\) be its family of constraint cost tables, with scopes \(\mathcal S\) treated as public or fixed. Fix observer coalition \(O\) and protocol \(\Pi\). Perfect valuation privacy holds relative to an admissible relation \(\sim_F\) if every \(I\sim_F I'\) having identical public information and prescribed outputs, but possibly different secret entries of the functions \(f_S\), satisfies \[V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I').\] Values explicitly revealed by an output are excluded from the secret component.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Valuation privacy makes admissible changes to secret constraint-table values indistinguishable while holding scopes, public information, and outputs fixed.
assumptions_latex: Constraint scopes are fixed or declared public.
Admissible valuation changes preserve prescribed outputs and public information.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(I\sim_F I'\) implies \(V_O^\Pi(I)\overset{d}{=}V_O^\Pi(I')\) under the stated public-information condition.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The selected valuation-indistinguishability notion requires a DCOP privacy source. In addition, statement_latex contains the undefined and undelimited command \tempeq after \(I\), violating the safe-LaTeX and explicit-delimiter requirements; this must be removed when a sourced replacement is prepared.

children.title: Constraint–Valuation Linkage Leakage
children.top_down_role: Leakage created by associating protected constraints with their evaluations.

knowledge_statements.title: Constraint–Valuation Linkage Leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information revealed about which secret valuation belongs to which constraint scope or identifier.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(C\) denote random secret constraint identifiers or scopes, let \(F\) denote their random valuation tables, and let \(L\) be the hidden association pairing elements of \(C\) with elements of \(F\). Given public information \(P\) and observer view \(V_O\), constraint–valuation linkage leakage is \[\mathsf{Leak}_{C\text{-}F}(O)=I(L;V_O\mid P,C,F).\] Conditioning on \(C\) and \(F\) isolates disclosure of their pairing from disclosure of either collection itself. Zero leakage is equivalent to conditional independence \(L\perp V_O\mid(P,C,F)\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Constraint–valuation linkage leakage measures information the observer learns about pairing constraint identities or scopes with valuation tables.
assumptions_latex: \(L\), \(C\), \(F\), \(P\), and \(V_O\) have a joint distribution.
The conditional mutual information is well-defined.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathsf{Leak}_{C\text{-}F}(O)=I(L;V_O\mid P,C,F)\), vanishing iff \(L\perp V_O\mid(P,C,F)\).

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The conditional-mutual-information formula is one possible leakage measure, but the random collections C and F and association L are not formalized sufficiently to show that L remains nontrivial after conditioning on C and F. A DCOP-specific source is required.

children.title: Decision Privacy
children.top_down_role: Protection of private choices made during distributed optimization.

assumptions_latex: A DCOP instance induces a protocol execution with public information \(P\), authorized output \(Y\), and adversarial view \(V\).
The protected local decision is a random variable \(D_i\) taking values in a finite domain \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Decision privacy holds exactly when the adversarial view reveals no information about \(D_i\) beyond the public information and authorized output.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional-independence formulation of information-theoretic privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information-theoretic privacy of one agent's selected decision, conditioned on authorized disclosure.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(D_i\in X_i\) be agent \(i\)'s protected decision, let \(P\) be public information, let \(Y\) be the authorized output, and let \(V\) be the view of the designated adversary after protocol execution. The protocol has perfect decision privacy for agent \(i\) when \[D_i\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}V\mid(P,Y),\] equivalently, for every \(d\in X_i\) and every \((p,y,v)\) of positive probability, \[\Pr[D_i=d\mid P=p,Y=y,V=v]=\Pr[D_i=d\mid P=p,Y=y].\] Computational decision privacy replaces equality by computational indistinguishability of the corresponding conditional view ensembles.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An adversary learns nothing about an agent's protected decision beyond what public information and the authorized output already disclose.
knowledge_statements.title: Decision Privacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the Decision Privacy leaf and the formulas are internally coherent, but no inspectable citation supports this particular conditional-independence definition or the stated computational variant in the DCOP setting. An authoritative DCOP privacy or secure-computation source with a specific locator is required.

children.title: Assignment Privacy
children.top_down_role: Protection of variable assignments or allocation outcomes.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has variables \(x_i\in X_i\) and final assignment \(A=(x_i)_{i\in N}\).
A protected coordinate set \(S\subseteq N\) and an adversarial view \(V\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Assignment privacy requires executions with equally authorized outputs and different protected assignments to induce indistinguishable adversarial views.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: indistinguishability formulation of assignment privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Privacy of one or more coordinates of the final joint DCOP assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(A=(x_i)_{i\in N}\in\prod_{i\in N}X_i\) be the final DCOP assignment and let \(A_S\) denote the coordinates protected from an adversary. Given public information \(P\) and authorized output \(Y\), perfect assignment privacy holds when \[A_S\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}V\mid(P,Y).\] In a computational formulation, for any two admissible instances whose public data and authorized outputs agree but whose protected assignments are \(a_S\) and \(a'_S\), the induced view ensembles \(V(a_S)\) and \(V(a'_S)\) are computationally indistinguishable. Coordinates explicitly included in \(Y\) are not protected by this definition.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Protected coordinates of the final joint assignment remain hidden except for information deliberately exposed by the authorized output.
knowledge_statements.title: Assignment Privacy

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the Assignment Privacy leaf, but the distinction from sibling Decision Privacy and the combination of conditional independence with an instance-pair computational formulation are unsupported. A source must establish the protected assignment semantics, admissible-instance relation, and authorized-output convention.

children.title: Temporal Assignment Leakage
children.top_down_role: Leakage arising from observing assignment changes over time.

assumptions_latex: A protocol produces a time-indexed transcript \(V_{0:T}=(V_0,\ldots,V_T)\).
The protected assignment process is \(A_{0:T}=(A_0,\ldots,A_T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Temporal leakage is the additional information about the assignment trajectory contained in the transcript beyond public information and authorized output.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional mutual information as transcript leakage
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Information leakage from intermediate and repeated assignments, including trajectories hidden by final-output privacy.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For horizon \(T\), define the temporal assignment leakage of an execution by \[L_T=I(A_{0:T};V_{0:T}\mid P,Y),\] where \(P\) is public information and \(Y\) is the authorized output. Perfect temporal assignment privacy holds when \(L_T=0\) for every finite \(T\). Incremental leakage at round \(t\) is \[\ell_t=I(A_{0:T};V_t\mid P,Y,V_{0:t-1}),\] and the chain rule gives \(L_T=\sum_{t=0}^{T}\ell_t\). Thus privacy of the final assignment alone does not imply temporal privacy when intermediate messages reveal rejected values, update times, or assignment changes.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Temporal leakage measures what a transcript reveals about intermediate and repeated assignments, not merely the final assignment.
knowledge_statements.title: Temporal Assignment Leakage

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role and mutual-information formulas fit Temporal Assignment Leakage, but no source supports this specific DCOP trajectory model, transcript scope, or use of every finite horizon as the privacy condition. A DCOP-specific or directly applicable information-leakage citation with a precise locator is required.

top_down_textbook_witnesses.source: Privacy of Existence of Secrets: Introducing Steganographic DCOPs and Revisiting DCOP Frameworks
top_down_textbook_witnesses.source_title: Privacy of Existence of Secrets: Introducing Steganographic DCOPs and Revisiting DCOP Frameworks

assumptions_latex: Instances are related by an adjacency relation \(\sim_s\) that changes only whether secret \(s\) exists.
The adversary observes a randomized protocol view \(V\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Existence privacy bounds how much the view distribution can change when the secret is inserted or removed.

notation.meaning: neighboring instances differing in secret existence

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: neighboring-instance formulation adapted from differential privacy
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Hides whether a designated private variable, constraint, agent, or fact exists in the DCOP instance.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Fix a secret \(s\) and let \(I\sim_s I'\) mean that admissible DCOP instances \(I\) and \(I'\) have identical public components and differ only by the presence versus absence of \(s\). A randomized protocol provides \((\varepsilon,\delta)\)-privacy of secret existence when, for every such pair and every measurable set \(E\) of adversarial views, \[\Pr[V(I)\in E]\le e^{\varepsilon}\Pr[V(I')\in E]+\delta\] and the same inequality holds with \(I\) and \(I'\) exchanged. Perfect existence privacy is the case \(\varepsilon=\delta=0\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Adding or removing a protected secret changes the adversary's view distribution by at most the specified privacy allowance.
knowledge_statements.title: Privacy of Secret Existence

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the leaf, and the symmetric differential-privacy-style inequality is mathematically recognizable. However, no citation supports importing this adjacency model into DCOP secret-existence privacy, and the scope ambiguously groups variables, constraints, agents, and facts whose insertion or removal may require different admissibility conditions.

assumptions_latex: Every agent follows the prescribed protocol and records its complete local view.
The protected input components and authorized outputs are specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Privacy against an honest-but-curious agent is simulation of its real view from its own input and authorized output alone.

notation.meaning: view of agent i in a real execution
input locally known to agent i

knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semi-honest adversary model specialized to agents participating in a DCOP protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: An honest-but-curious agent \(i\) executes every instruction of protocol \(\Pi\), uses prescribed randomness, and sends prescribed messages, but retains its input, randomness, received messages, and outputs for inference. Protocol \(\Pi\) preserves privacy against such an agent when there exists a probabilistic polynomial-time simulator \(S_i\) such that, for every admissible instance \(I\), \[S_i(I_i,Y_i)\mathrel{\approx_c}\operatorname{View}_i^{\Pi}(I),\] where \(I_i\) is agent \(i\)'s legitimate local input, \(Y_i\) is its authorized output, and \(\approx_c\) denotes computational indistinguishability. An information-theoretic version replaces \(\approx_c\) by equality in distribution.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A compliant but inquisitive agent can reconstruct no more from execution than from its legitimate input and authorized output.
knowledge_statements.title: Honest-but-Curious Agents

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the Honest-but-Curious Agents adversary-regime leaf. The simulation condition is standard in secure computation, but no authoritative citation is supplied for its exact formulation or specialization to DCOP protocols, including what belongs to an agent's legitimate input and authorized output.

assumptions_latex: A coalition \(C\subseteq N\) pools all members' inputs, randomness, messages, and outputs.
Coalition members otherwise follow the prescribed protocol.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Coalition privacy is simulation of the coalition's joint view from exactly its collective legitimate information.
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Semi-honest coalitions that combine their complete protocol views to infer other agents' secrets.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a coalition \(C\subseteq N\), define its joint view by the tuple of all members' inputs, random coins, sent and received messages, and outputs. Protocol \(\Pi\) is private against coalitions of size at most \(t\) when, for every \(C\) with \(|C|\le t\), there exists a probabilistic polynomial-time simulator \(S_C\) satisfying \[S_C(I_C,Y_C)\mathrel{\approx_c}\operatorname{View}_C^{\Pi}(I)\] for every admissible instance \(I\). Here \(I_C\) and \(Y_C\) contain precisely the coalition's legitimate inputs and authorized outputs; information logically implied by them is not counted as leakage.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Even after pooling their records, up to t colluding agents learn no more than their combined legitimate inputs and outputs imply.
knowledge_statements.title: Colluding Agents

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits the Colluding Agents leaf, and the bounded semi-honest coalition formulation is coherent. No source supports the selected coalition regime, threshold semantics, or joint-view definition in the relevant DCOP context, so the mathematical scope cannot be confirmed.

assumptions_latex: A mediator participates in protocol \(\Pi\) but is not authorized to learn protected agent data.
Its legitimate input \(I_M\) and authorized output \(Y_M\) are explicitly specified.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Mediator privacy requires its complete execution view to be simulatable from only its authorized information.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: simulation security for a semi-honest intermediary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Privacy from a semi-honest coordinating service that observes mediation messages but lacks access authorization.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let mediator \(M\) coordinate some DCOP messages or computations without authorization to inspect protected inputs. In the semi-honest model, \(M\) follows protocol \(\Pi\) but records its input, randomness, messages, and output. The mediation is private from \(M\) when a probabilistic polynomial-time simulator \(S_M\) exists such that, for every admissible instance \(I\), \[S_M(I_M,Y_M)\mathrel{\approx_c}\operatorname{View}_M^{\Pi}(I).\] If \(M\) may deviate from \(\Pi\), this condition is insufficient; the model must additionally specify correctness, input validation, and security against malicious behavior.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: An untrusted coordinator's entire view must reveal no more than its explicitly authorized input and output.
knowledge_statements.title: Untrusted Mediators

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits an adversary-regime leaf, but the title does not itself fix a semi-honest mediator model. The record correctly notes that malicious mediation needs stronger conditions, yet no source establishes which regime and view semantics belong to this DCOP container.

assumptions_latex: A secret \(S\), public information \(P\), authorized output \(Y\), and transcript \(T\) are jointly distributed.
The adversary applies any estimator measurable with respect to \((P,Y,T)\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Transcript-based inference leakage is quantified by posterior change or by the adversary's gain in optimal prediction success.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: conditional mutual-information and inference-gain formulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Passive inference about DCOP secrets from message contents, order, sizes, senders, or timing.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Define information leakage from transcript \(T\) about secret \(S\) by \[L=I(S;T\mid P,Y).\] For finite \(S\), the associated optimal guessing gain is \[G=\max_g\Pr[g(P,Y,T)=S]-\max_h\Pr[h(P,Y)=S],\] where \(g\) and \(h\) range over all estimators. Perfect transcript privacy implies \(L=0\), equivalently \(S\mathbin{\perp\!\!\!\perp}T\mid(P,Y)\), and consequently \(G=0\). The transcript includes every observable feature declared by the threat model; excluding metadata such as timing or sender identity narrows the resulting guarantee.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Transcript inference is the extra ability to learn or predict a secret after observing execution messages and metadata.
knowledge_statements.title: Transcript-Based Inference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The definition role fits Transcript-Based Inference, and the conditional mutual-information and guessing-gain quantities are internally consistent for finite secrets. A source is still required to support these as the intended DCOP leakage objects and to establish whether message metadata is included in the transcript.

assumptions_latex: The search protocol explores a finite DCOP search space and has a specified authorized output \(Y\).
A threat class \(\mathcal A\) and protected instance data \(S\) are fixed.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: A privacy-preserving search must retain search correctness while making each allowed adversarial view simulatable without protected data.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correctness-plus-simulation specification for private search
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Functional specification for distributed enumeration, pruning, or branch search with protected DCOP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A protocol \(\Pi\) is a privacy-preserving search method for a DCOP when it satisfies both requirements. Correctness requires that, upon termination, its output \(Y\) is an optimal feasible assignment and objective value, or the explicitly requested search result, except with stated error probability. Privacy requires that, for every adversary \(A\in\mathcal A\), there exists a simulator \(S_A\) such that \[S_A(I_A,Y_A)\mathrel{\approx}\operatorname{View}_A^{\Pi}(I).\] Initialization, node expansion, bound computation, pruning, and termination messages must all be included in \(\operatorname{View}_A^{\Pi}(I)\); hiding only the final search result is insufficient.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Private search must return the prescribed DCOP solution while exposing no protected information through exploration, pruning, or termination behavior.
knowledge_statements.title: Privacy-Preserving Search

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role is suitable for the Privacy-Preserving Search method-family leaf. However, no source supports the proposed correctness-plus-simulation specification, and the relation denoted by \(\approx\) is not defined as computational, statistical, or exact. Source-backed threat, leakage, correctness, and indistinguishability models are required.

assumptions_latex: A distributed inference task computes an authorized statistic \(Y=F(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\).
Each allowed adversary has a defined legitimate input and output.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Privacy-preserving inference computes the authorized statistic while making the adversary's execution view simulatable from legitimate information alone.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: secure-computation specification for distributed inference
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Secure evaluation of DCOP-derived statistics, bounds, beliefs, or aggregate costs without exposing private inputs.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(F\) be an inference function on private local inputs \((I_1,\ldots,I_n)\), with authorized result \(Y=F(I_1,\ldots,I_n)\). A protocol \(\Pi_F\) is privacy-preserving when it computes \(Y\) with the declared correctness probability and, for every allowed adversary \(A\), admits a simulator satisfying \[S_A(I_A,Y_A)\mathrel{\approx}\operatorname{View}_A^{\Pi_F}(I_1,\ldots,I_n).\] The result \(Y_A\) may reveal consequences logically implied by the prescribed inference output; intermediate factors, partial aggregates, message schedules, and convergence traces are protected unless the disclosure policy explicitly authorizes them.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Private inference releases only the prescribed statistic and what it logically implies, while concealing intermediate and local data.
knowledge_statements.title: Privacy-Preserving Inference

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the Privacy-Preserving Inference method-family leaf, but the broad function-evaluation formulation is unsupported and may describe generic secure computation rather than the exact DCOP inference family. The meaning of \(\approx\), the allowed adversaries, and the authorized intermediate disclosures require a cited specification.

assumptions_latex: Agents submit protected inputs to a mediation protocol producing authorized output \(Y\).
The mediator and any permitted coalition are included in a threat class \(\mathcal A\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Private mediation requires correct coordination and simulation security for every designated observer or coalition.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: correctness-plus-simulation specification for private mediation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Coordination through a mediator without granting it unrestricted access to agents' private DCOP data.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: A mediation protocol \(\Pi_M\) is privacy-preserving for threat class \(\mathcal A\) when it terminates with the prescribed feasible or optimal mediation result \(Y\), subject to its declared error model, and when every \(A\in\mathcal A\) has a simulator such that \[S_A(I_A,Y_A)\mathrel{\approx}\operatorname{View}_A^{\Pi_M}(I).\] The view includes submissions, mediator state, recommendations, retries, and metadata available to \(A\). If the mediator may deviate, privacy must be paired with verifiable correctness or malicious-security guarantees; confidentiality against a compliant mediator alone does not establish privacy-preserving mediation in that regime.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Private mediation coordinates a correct DCOP outcome while limiting what the mediator and permitted coalitions can infer.
knowledge_statements.title: Privacy-Preserving Mediation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The principle role fits the Privacy-Preserving Mediation method-family leaf. No source establishes this particular combination of mediation correctness, simulation privacy, metadata coverage, and malicious-security qualifications, and \(\approx\) is left without a defined indistinguishability regime.
