knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If some modeled-objective minimizer is not a true application-objective minimizer, exact DCOP solution does not guarantee application optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(X\neq\varnothing\) and both objectives attain minima on \(X\).
The solver is required to optimize the application criterion \(G\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_X F\not\subseteq\operatorname*{argmin}_X G\) implies that exact minimization of \(F\) is insufficient.
review_flags: The supplied objective locator does not establish this DCOP semantic boundary.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The argmin-set condition correctly expresses failure of guaranteed application optimality and fits the container, but the supplied inventory does not support this DCOP semantic boundary.

knowledge_statements.title: Ownership-Distorting Reformulations
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Central equivalence does not ensure distributed implementability under factor ownership constraints.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex:
Consider a centralized-equivalent reformulation with factors \(g_a\) and ownership map \(o(a)\). Let \(K_i\) denote all information agent \(i\) may lawfully obtain. The reformulation is not locally implementable under that ownership assignment if, for some factor \(a\), there exist feasible assignments \(x,y\) indistinguishable from \(K_{o(a)}\) but satisfying \(g_a(x)
eq g_a(y)\). Then owner \(o(a)\) cannot evaluate its assigned factor correctly on both assignments, even if the reformulated centralized objective equals the original objective everywhere.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A centrally equivalent reformulation fails distributively when a designated factor owner cannot distinguish assignments on which its assigned factor has different values.
assumptions_latex: The reformulated and original centralized objectives agree on every feasible assignment.
Agent information is restricted to the sets \(K_i\).
Some owned factor varies across assignments indistinguishable to its owner.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The assigned factor decomposition is not locally evaluable under the stated ownership and information policy.

notation.meaning: factor introduced or reassigned by the reformulation
agent designated to own factor a

review_flags: The supplied reformulation locator does not address distributed factor ownership or information constraints.

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The proposed ownership failure boundary is plausible, but indistinguishability with respect to K_i is not formally defined and no source supports the distributed factor-ownership conclusion.

children.title: Strategic Manipulation
children.top_down_role: Misreporting, selective disclosure, utility manipulation, plus opportunistic protocol participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Strategic Manipulation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Profitable misreporting by self-interested agents in a direct DCOP protocol.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a direct protocol choose an assignment \(x=M(\hat\theta_1,\ldots,\hat\theta_n)\) from reported types, where agent \(i\) has true type \(\theta_i\) and utility \(u_i(x;\theta_i)\). Strategic manipulation occurs when there exist \(i\), \(\theta_i\), \(\hat\theta_i\neq\theta_i\), and reports \(\hat\theta_{-i}\) such that \[u_i\bigl(M(\hat\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i});\theta_i\bigr)>u_i\bigl(M(\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i});\theta_i\bigr).\] A conventional DCOP solution computed from the reported costs then need not optimize the objective induced by the agents' true types.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Strategic manipulation exists when an agent can obtain greater true utility by reporting false private information, so reported-objective optimality need not imply true-objective optimality.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) selects an assignment from reported agent types.
Each agent may report a type different from its true type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is manipulable, and its reported DCOP optimum need not be a true-type optimum.

notation.meaning: Agent i's true and reported types

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: profitable-misreport predicate is the standard direct-mechanism definition of manipulation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The profitable-misreport predicate fits the Strategic Manipulation failure-boundary leaf, but no inspectable citation is supplied. A source must also support the final claim connecting utility manipulation to failure of true-type aggregate-objective optimality, which requires an explicit relationship between utilities, types, and that aggregate objective.

children.title: Non-Cooperative Participation
children.top_down_role: Withholding effort, refusal to follow coordination outcomes, unilateral deviation, plus adversarial participation.

knowledge_statements.title: Non-Cooperative Participation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Failure of the obedient-agent assumption when participation or prescribed actions are voluntary.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a protocol prescribe strategy \(s_i^*\) to each agent and produce outcome \(x(s)\), with utility \(u_i(x(s))\). Non-cooperative participation invalidates the standard DCOP execution model whenever some agent can refuse participation or choose \(s_i\neq s_i^*\) and obtain \[u_i\bigl(x(s_i,s_{-i}^*)\bigr)>u_i\bigl(x(s_i^*,s_{-i}^*)\bigr).\] In that case the prescribed strategy profile is not a Nash equilibrium, so algorithmic convergence under obedient execution does not establish implementation of the computed assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: If an agent benefits by refusing or deviating from its prescribed behavior, obedient DCOP convergence does not guarantee that the computed assignment will be implemented.
assumptions_latex: Agents control whether or how they execute their prescribed protocol actions.
Utilities need not equal the aggregate DCOP objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(s^*\) is not a Nash equilibrium and obedient-execution guarantees do not apply.

notation.meaning: Outcome induced by strategy profile s

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: unilateral profitable deviation is the standard boundary between obedient distributed optimization and non-cooperative implementation
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The unilateral profitable-deviation condition correctly identifies failure of the prescribed profile to be a Nash equilibrium and fits this failure-boundary leaf. The record nevertheless has no source with a specific locator supporting its application to obedient DCOP execution and implementation.

children.title: Incentive Compatibility Failure
children.top_down_role: Conditions where cooperative optimization objectives do not align with participant incentives.

knowledge_statements.title: Incentive Compatibility Failure
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Formal failure of dominant-strategy truthfulness for a direct DCOP mechanism.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a direct mechanism \(M\), dominant-strategy incentive compatibility requires, for every agent \(i\), true type \(\theta_i\), alternative report \(r_i\), and reports \(r_{-i}\), \[u_i\bigl(M(\theta_i,r_{-i});\theta_i\bigr)\ge u_i\bigl(M(r_i,r_{-i});\theta_i\bigr).\] Incentive compatibility fails precisely when the negation holds: there exist \(i,\theta_i,r_i,r_{-i}\) for which the displayed inequality is strict in the reverse direction. Optimization of reported aggregate cost alone does not exclude this failure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Dominant-strategy incentive compatibility fails exactly when some agent can improve its true utility through a false report for some reports of the other agents.
assumptions_latex: \(M\) is a direct mechanism defined on reported types.
Agent utility is evaluated using its true type.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(M\) is not dominant-strategy incentive compatible iff a profitable false report exists.

notation.meaning: True type and alternative report of agent i

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the quantified truthful-report inequality is the standard dominant-strategy incentive-compatibility predicate
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The quantified inequality and its negation are the standard dominant-strategy incentive-compatibility test, but the record has no inspectable source. Moreover, this terminal container concerns a failure phenomenon, so failure_boundary is a better mathematical role than condition; that correction should be made after authoritative support is supplied.

children.title: Enforcement Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits arising when compliance, truthful reporting, or outcome adoption cannot be ensured.

knowledge_statements.title: Enforcement Boundary
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Separates computation of an assignment from enforceable implementation by autonomous agents.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(x^*\) be a DCOP assignment and let \(a_i^*\) be the physical or protocol action required from agent \(i\) to implement it. Enforcement requires an admissible rule \(E\), such as verifiable sanctions or transfers, satisfying \[u_i(a_i^*,a_{-i}^*;E)\ge u_i(a_i,a_{-i}^*;E)\quad\text{for every feasible }a_i.\] If actions or outcomes are unverifiable and no such rule belongs to the application model, the DCOP solver certifies only computational optimality of \(x^*\); it does not certify compliance or realization.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A computed assignment is enforceable only when available monitoring, sanctions, or transfers make every prescribed action at least as attractive as unilateral deviation.
assumptions_latex: Agents autonomously choose implementation actions.
Only rules admitted by the application model may be used for enforcement.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: Absent an admissible \(E\) satisfying the deviation inequalities, optimal assignment computation does not guarantee implementation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: implementation requires prescribed actions to satisfy incentive constraints under an available enforcement institution
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The distinction between computational optimality and implementability fits the Enforcement Boundary leaf, but the proposed rule E and deviation inequalities instantiate a particular enforcement model without cited support. An authoritative source must specify the monitoring, sanction, transfer, or implementation framework under which this formulation is valid.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralization Disguised as Distribution
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Detects architectures whose execution is dispersed but whose information and optimization are centralized.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider a purported distributed solver with local data \(D_1,\ldots,D_n\). It is centralized in the information-and-control sense if one coordinator receives sufficient statistics \(T_i(D_i)\) satisfying \[F(x;D_1,\ldots,D_n)=\Phi\bigl(x,T_1(D_1),\ldots,T_n(D_n)\bigr)\] for every feasible \(x\), computes the complete selected assignment \(x^*\), and subordinate agents merely transmit data or execute assigned values. Parallel communication or execution does not remove this boundary: the decisive optimization state and authority remain at one site.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A system remains centralized when one coordinator receives enough information to reconstruct the objective and chooses the entire assignment, even if communication or execution is dispersed.
assumptions_latex: A single coordinator has global decision authority.
Transmitted statistics suffice to evaluate the complete objective.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The architecture is centralized with respect to information aggregation and assignment selection.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: distribution of execution is distinct from distribution of information and decision authority
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The record fits the Centralization Disguised as Distribution failure-boundary topic, but the sufficient-statistic criterion is an uncited formalization rather than a source-backed standard definition. A specific source is needed for the information-and-control characterization and its claimed boundary.

children.title: Centralized COP Interface
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between distributed constraint models plus centralized constraint optimization representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralized COP Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Forgets agent ownership while preserving the deterministic finite-domain optimization problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let a finite DCOP have variables \(X=\{x_1,\ldots,x_m\}\), finite domains \(D_j\), agents \(A\), ownership map \(\alpha:X\to A\), and cost functions \(f_k:\prod_{x_j\in S_k}D_j\to\mathbb R\cup\{+\infty\}\). Its centralized COP interface is \[\min_{x\in\prod_{j=1}^m D_j}F(x),\qquad F(x)=\sum_k f_k(x_{S_k}).\] The interface retains variables, domains, scopes, feasibility encoded by infinite cost, and objective values, while omitting ownership and communication structure.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite DCOP becomes a centralized constraint optimization problem by retaining variables and local costs, summing those costs, and forgetting agent ownership and communication structure.
assumptions_latex: All variable domains and cost-function scopes are finite.
The DCOP objective is additive and minimized.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The centralized COP and the DCOP have the same feasible assignments, objective values, and minimizers.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a finite additive DCOP reduces to a centralized COP by forgetting ownership and summing scoped costs
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The representation correctly describes the centralized finite additive COP obtained by forgetting ownership and communication metadata, and representation is the appropriate content kind. No inspectable source with a section, theorem, definition, or page locator is supplied.

children.title: WCSP Interface
children.top_down_role: Correspondence between DCOP cost structures plus weighted constraint satisfaction representations.

knowledge_statements.title: WCSP Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Cost-function translation between finite minimization DCOPs and weighted constraint satisfaction.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For a finite minimization DCOP with scoped costs \(f_k\), choose a WCSP top cost \(\top\) and map every prohibited tuple to \(\top\), while mapping each finite tuple cost to its value in a totally ordered additive cost domain. Define truncated aggregation by \(a\oplus b=\min\{\top,a+b\}\). The corresponding WCSP objective is \[C(x)=\bigoplus_k f_k(x_{S_k}).\] If no feasible aggregate reaches \(\top\), ordering assignments by \(C\) agrees with ordering them by the DCOP's summed cost.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite DCOP is represented as a WCSP by treating each local cost as a weighted constraint, prohibited tuples as top cost, and aggregating costs by truncated addition.
assumptions_latex: Domains and scoped cost tables are finite.
Finite DCOP costs embed order-preservingly below \(\top\).
No feasible aggregate saturates at \(\top\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin}_x C(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_k f_k(x_{S_k})\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite additive cost functions are the standard weighted-constraint representation of a tabular DCOP
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The truncated-addition construction is mathematically plausible under the stated nonsaturation assumption and fits the WCSP Interface representation leaf. A specific WCSP source is required to support the top-cost convention, admissible cost domain, and optimizer-preservation conditions.

children.title: Centralization Mapping
children.top_down_role: Preservation of objectives, feasibility, ownership, locality, plus solution interpretation under centralized reformulation.

knowledge_statements.title: Centralization Mapping
knowledge_statements.scope_note: A value-preserving forgetful map from finite DCOP instances to centralized COP instances.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Write a finite DCOP instance as \(I=(A,X,D,\alpha,\mathcal F,G)\), where \(A\) is the agent set, \(\alpha\) records ownership, \(\mathcal F\) is the family of scoped costs, and \(G\) is the permitted communication graph. Define the centralization map by \[\mathcal C(I)=(X,D,\mathcal F),\qquad F_I(x)=\sum_{f\in\mathcal F}f(x_{\operatorname{scope}(f)}).\] For every assignment \(x\), \(\mathcal C(I)\) preserves \(F_I(x)\), hence preserves feasibility and optimal assignments under the infinite-cost convention.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Centralization deletes agents, ownership, and communication restrictions but retains variables, domains, and cost functions, thereby preserving assignment costs and optimizers.
assumptions_latex: The instance has finite domains and additive scoped costs.
A prohibited tuple is represented by cost \(+\infty\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmin} I=\operatorname*{argmin}\mathcal C(I)\) as sets of variable assignments.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: forgetting ownership and communication metadata preserves the underlying additive optimization problem
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The forgetful, value-preserving map fits the Centralization Mapping representation leaf and is internally coherent under the infinite-cost convention. It lacks an inspectable citation supporting the DCOP-to-centralized-COP mapping and preservation claim.

children.title: Distribution Information Loss
children.top_down_role: Ownership, privacy, communication, trust, plus execution semantics omitted by centralized representations.

knowledge_statements.title: Distribution Information Loss
knowledge_statements.scope_note: The centralization map is generally non-injective because it forgets distributed semantics.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let \(\mathcal C\) be the centralization map that retains \((X,D,\mathcal F)\) and discards the agent set, ownership map, permitted communication graph, and privacy labels. There can exist distinct DCOP instances \(I\neq I'\) with different ownership or communication structures but \[\mathcal C(I)=\mathcal C(I').\] Consequently, no reconstruction map depending only on the centralized COP can recover the original distributed structure for every instance. Optimization equivalence under \(\mathcal C\) therefore does not imply equivalence of privacy exposure, communication feasibility, or agent authority.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Different distributed instances can yield the same centralized COP, so centralization irreversibly loses ownership, communication, privacy, and authority information.
assumptions_latex: \(\mathcal C\) omits ownership and communication metadata.
At least two admissible distributed structures share the same variables, domains, and costs.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\mathcal C\) is non-injective and has no universal inverse on distributed instance structure.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a projection that deletes ownership and communication fields is non-injective whenever those fields can vary independently
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The non-injectivity conclusion follows from the stated ability to vary discarded metadata and fits the Distribution Information Loss property leaf. No source is provided for the distributed semantics being discarded or for the claimed consequences concerning privacy, communication feasibility, and authority.

knowledge_statements.title: Graphical-Model Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Represents an additive finite DCOP as a factor graph and equivalent Gibbs MAP problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given finite variables \(X\) and costs \(f_k(x_{S_k})\), construct a factor graph with one variable node per \(x_j\), one factor node per \(f_k\), and edges joining \(f_k\) to variables in \(S_k\). For any \(\beta>0\), define \(\psi_k(x_{S_k})=\exp(-\beta f_k(x_{S_k}))\), with \(\exp(-\beta\cdot+\infty)=0\), and \[p(x)=Z^{-1}\prod_k\psi_k(x_{S_k}).\] Whenever \(Z>0\), maximum-probability assignments of \(p\) are exactly minimum-total-cost DCOP assignments.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Local DCOP costs become graphical-model factors through exponentiation; the resulting Gibbs distribution has MAP assignments exactly equal to minimum-cost DCOP assignments.
assumptions_latex: Domains are finite.
At least one assignment has finite total cost.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_x p(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x\sum_k f_k(x_{S_k})\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: exponentiated negative additive costs yield a Gibbs factorization whose MAP and minimum-energy assignments coincide
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The Gibbs-factor construction and MAP/minimum-cost equivalence are precise for finite domains with a positive normalizer, and representation fits this interface topic. The record has no specific source supporting the factor-graph construction and energy-to-probability correspondence.

children.top_down_role: Integer formulations, polyhedral theory, cutting planes, branching, fixed-dimension algorithms, and decomposition or callback mechanisms remain in the integer-optimization chapter.

knowledge_statements.title: Integer-Optimization Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Exact configuration-based integer formulation of a finite tabular DCOP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each variable \(x_j\) and value \(v\in D_j\), introduce \(y_{jv}\in\{0,1\}\). For each cost table \(f_k\) and local tuple \(s\in\prod_{x_j\in S_k}D_j\), introduce \(\lambda_{ks}\in\{0,1\}\). Impose \[\sum_{v\in D_j}y_{jv}=1,\qquad \sum_s\lambda_{ks}=1,\qquad \sum_{s:s_j=v}\lambda_{ks}=y_{jv}.\] Minimizing \(\sum_k\sum_s f_k(s)\lambda_{ks}\), after excluding forbidden tuples, is an exact integer-linear formulation: integral feasible points correspond bijectively to DCOP assignments and have identical objective values.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: One-hot variable indicators and consistent local-configuration indicators produce an exact integer-linear model of any finite tabular DCOP.
assumptions_latex: Every domain and cost table is finite.
Forbidden tuples are removed or fixed to zero.
All indicator variables are binary.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The integer formulation and the DCOP have corresponding feasible assignments and equal optimal values.

notation.meaning: Indicator that variable j takes value v
Indicator that factor k selects local tuple s

source_refs.locator: 1.1 Classification of Nonlinear Integer Programming Formulations p. 2

review_flags: locator supports integer-formulation context; exact configuration formulation requires source confirmation

The consistency equations also need explicit quantification over k, x_j in S_k, and v in D_j. Because the immutable role reserves integer formulations for the integer-optimization chapter, evidence must additionally establish that this record is an interface mapping rather than formulation theory improperly placed in this terminal container.

knowledge_statements.title: Decision-Theory Interface
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Interprets deterministic DCOP minimization as a cooperative common-payoff decision problem.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Let agents jointly choose components of assignment \(x\), and let the deterministic DCOP cost be \(F(x)=\sum_k f_k(x_{S_k})\). Define a common team utility by \[U_i(x)=-F(x)\qquad\text{for every agent }i.\] Then every team-optimal joint decision maximizes each common utility and minimizes the DCOP cost. This equivalence requires aligned utilities and a deterministic, single-stage outcome; heterogeneous preferences, private strategic types, sequential information, or uncertainty introduce decision-theoretic structure not represented by the basic DCOP objective.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A deterministic DCOP is a cooperative team decision problem when every agent shares utility equal to negative total cost; preference conflict or uncertainty breaks this direct equivalence.
assumptions_latex: The outcome is deterministic and single-stage.
All agents share the same utility \(-F\).
The joint feasible decisions equal the DCOP assignments.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: \(\operatorname*{argmax}_x U_i(x)=\operatorname*{argmin}_x F(x)\) for every agent \(i\).
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: minimizing a deterministic common cost is equivalent to maximizing its negative as common team utility
auto_normalized: candidate_review without source_refs downgraded to needs_source

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The negative-common-cost construction is a coherent deterministic common-payoff representation and fits the Decision-Theory Interface leaf. No inspectable decision-theory or DCOP source is supplied for the team interpretation or for the stated limits involving heterogeneous preferences, strategic types, sequential information, and uncertainty.

children.title: Game-Theory Interface
children.top_down_role: Strategic-agent interpretations, equilibrium concepts, preference conflicts, plus decentralized choice.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite variable domains and objective \(F(x)=\sum_{k\in K} f_k(x_{S_k})\), which is minimized.
The variables are partitioned as \(X=\bigsqcup_{i\in N}X_i\), and player \(i\) may unilaterally change exactly the coordinates in \(X_i\).
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The induced game is an identical-interest exact-potential game with potential \(\Phi=-F\), and its pure Nash equilibria are precisely the assignments that are locally optimal against every single player's admissible block deviation.
review_flags: standard_field_rationale: finite DCOPs with partitioned variable control admit the stated identical-interest game representation
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Finite deterministic DCOP interpreted as a complete-information identical-interest game under block deviations.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Given the feasible joint assignments \(\mathcal X=\prod_{j\in X}D_j\), define a normal-form game whose players are \(N\), whose action set for player \(i\) is \(A_i=\prod_{j\in X_i}D_j\), and whose utilities satisfy \(u_i(x)=-F(x)\) for every \(i\in N\). Then \(\Phi(x)=-F(x)\) is an exact potential: for every unilateral deviation \(x_i'\in A_i\), \[u_i(x_i',x_{-i})-u_i(x_i,x_{-i})=\Phi(x_i',x_{-i})-\Phi(x_i,x_{-i}).\] Consequently, \(x^\star\) is a pure Nash equilibrium exactly when \(F(x^\star)\leq F(x_i',x_{-i}^\star)\) for every \(i\in N\) and \(x_i'\in A_i\).
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A finite DCOP with partitioned variable control becomes an identical-interest potential game; pure Nash equilibria are assignments immune to every agent's unilateral block change.
knowledge_statements.title: Game-Theory Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The identical-interest exact-potential representation and the block-deviation characterization of pure Nash equilibrium are mathematically coherent and fit the Game-Theory Interface container, but no inspectable citation supports the DCOP-to-game formulation.

children.title: Mechanism-Design Interface
children.top_down_role: Incentive structures, reporting behavior, allocation rules, payments, plus implementable outcomes.

assumptions_latex: Each agent \(i\) has type space \(\Theta_i\), quasilinear valuation \(v_i(o,\theta_i)\), and can report any \(\hat\theta_i\in\Theta_i\).
The reported DCOP determines an outcome rule \(g:\Theta\to O\), while transfers \(p_i:\Theta\to\mathbb R\) are specified separately.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The DCOP-based outcome rule and transfers define a dominant-strategy incentive-compatible direct mechanism exactly when the displayed report inequalities hold for every agent, true type, deviation, and reports of others.

notation.meaning: Outcome selected by solving the reported DCOP.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: dominant-strategy incentive compatibility is characterized by the direct-mechanism reporting inequalities
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Direct, quasilinear mechanism whose allocation rule is implemented by solving a report-dependent DCOP.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For reports \(\hat\theta=(\hat\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i})\), let the mechanism select \(g(\hat\theta)\) by solving the corresponding reported DCOP and assign utility \(U_i(\theta_i;\hat\theta)=v_i(g(\hat\theta),\theta_i)-p_i(\hat\theta)\). The interface is dominant-strategy incentive compatible if and only if, for every \(i\in N\), \(\theta_i,\hat\theta_i\in\Theta_i\), and \(\hat\theta_{-i}\in\Theta_{-i}\), \[v_i(g(\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i}),\theta_i)-p_i(\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i})\geq v_i(g(\hat\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i}),\theta_i)-p_i(\hat\theta_i,\hat\theta_{-i}).\] Optimization of the reported objective alone specifies \(g\), but does not by itself establish these inequalities.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: A report-dependent DCOP becomes a direct mechanism only after transfers and true-type utilities are specified; strategy-proofness requires every truthful report to dominate every misreport.
knowledge_statements.title: Mechanism-Design Interface

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The displayed inequality is the standard dominant-strategy incentive-compatibility condition and the condition kind fits the interface container. An authoritative citation is absent, and the notation describes p_i as a transfer paid to the agent while utility subtracts p_i; the source or record must clarify that p_i is instead a payment charged to the agent, or reverse the sign convention.

children.title: Cooperative-Strategic Translation
children.top_down_role: Mappings between cooperative DCOP objectives plus strategically motivated participant models.

assumptions_latex: The DCOP has finite domains, agent-partitioned variables \(X=\bigsqcup_{i\in N}X_i\), and finite global cost \(F\).
A feasible default assignment \(x^0\) is fixed, and a coalition may change only variables controlled by its members.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The characteristic function \(v(S)=c(\varnothing)-c(S)\) is the coalition's maximal cost reduction relative to the fixed default and defines a transferable-utility cooperative game on \(N\).

notation.meaning: Minimum cost achievable by coalition \(S\) with outsiders fixed.
Transferable coalition value measured as cost reduction.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: a baseline-relative coalition savings function translates a partitioned finite optimization problem into a TU game
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Baseline-relative TU translation with outsiders' variables fixed at a declared feasible assignment.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: For each coalition \(S\subseteq N\), define \(X_S=\bigcup_{i\in S}X_i\) and \[c(S)=\min\{F(x):x_j=x_j^0\text{ for every }j\in X\setminus X_S\}.\] Set \(c(\varnothing)=F(x^0)\) and define \(v:2^N\to\mathbb R\) by \[v(S)=c(\varnothing)-c(S).\] Then \((N,v)\) is a transferable-utility cooperative game representing the maximal reduction in DCOP cost attainable when exactly the agents in \(S\) may coordinate their controlled variables. The translation is relative to \(x^0\); changing the default assignment or the outsiders' response convention can change every coalition value.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Fixing outsiders at a baseline turns each coalition's best attainable DCOP cost reduction into a transferable-utility characteristic value.
knowledge_statements.title: Cooperative-Strategic Translation

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The baseline-relative coalition-savings construction is internally consistent, gives v(emptyset)=0, and appropriately serves as a cooperative-strategic representation. No inspectable source supports this particular DCOP-to-transferable-utility translation or its stated interpretation.

children.title: Incentive Representation Boundary
children.top_down_role: Limits of DCOP representations for private incentives, equilibrium requirements, transfers, or enforceability.

assumptions_latex: A one-agent reported DCOP has report set \(\Theta=\{0,2\}\), outcomes \(O=\{a,b\}\), and selection rule \(g(0)=a\), \(g(2)=b\).
There are no transfers, and the reported DCOP does not encode the agent's true outcome utility.
knowledge_statements.conclusion_latex: The same report-dependent DCOP rule \(g\) is truthful under \(u^{+}\) and manipulable under \(u^{-}\); therefore its objective and constraints alone cannot certify incentive compatibility.

notation.meaning: Outcome selected from the reported DCOP.
Utility profile aligned with the selected outcome.
Utility profile preferring the outcome selected by the opposite report.

review_flags: standard_field_rationale: the explicit pair of utility completions demonstrates underdetermination of incentives by an allocation objective
knowledge_statements.scope_note: Counterexample showing that report-dependent optimization does not determine incentives without true utilities or payments.
knowledge_statements.statement_latex: Consider two utility completions of the same rule \(g\). In the aligned completion, let \(u_0^{+}(a)=u_2^{+}(b)=1\) and \(u_0^{+}(b)=u_2^{+}(a)=0\); truthful reporting is optimal for both types. In the reversed completion, let \(u_0^{-}(a)=u_2^{-}(b)=0\) and \(u_0^{-}(b)=u_2^{-}(a)=1\). Then type \(0\) gains by reporting \(2\), and type \(2\) gains by reporting \(0\). Both completions have identical reported DCOP objectives, constraints, feasible outcomes, and selection rule. Hence those optimization data do not determine whether truthful reporting is an equilibrium or dominant strategy.
knowledge_statements.statement_plain: Identical DCOP allocation data can support either truthful or manipulable behavior under different true utilities, so incentive compatibility is not representable without utility or payment information.
knowledge_statements.title: Incentive Representation Boundary

intermediate_metadata.review_comment: The explicit utility completions correctly demonstrate that identical allocation data can yield truthful or manipulable reporting, and failure_boundary is the correct kind for this terminal container. Nevertheless, the record supplies no inspectable citation for the incentive-representation boundary it formalizes.
